headings.text: Transforming Insurance Claims: Three Strategic Imperatives for Insurers

paragraphs: HomeBlogs
HomeBlogs
6 Minutes Read
Claims
Raghavendra "Raghu" Aithal
SVP, ClaimsValueMomentum
Claims

The insurance industry is at a crossroads when it comes to managing claims. A staggering 80 cents of every dollar earned on premiums is typically funneled into claims, which highlights the growing pressure insurers face to improve their claims processes. But cost isn’t the only reason insurers should prioritize transforming their claims operations: Theclaims experienceremains a vital touchpoint between insurers and their customers.

Unfortunately, it’s also the source of the majority of consumer complaints in the industry,70.9%, in fact, reflecting a significant opportunity for improvement. Claims management is one of the most important levers for insurers to generate value and strengthen customer relationships. As the insurance ecosystem continues to evolve, transforming the claims value chain is no longer optional — it’s imperative for staying competitive.

The insurance industry is grappling with a growing disconnect between customer expectations andthe current state of claimsmanagement. Between the need for more digital experiences, growing threats within the insurance industry, and a reliance on legacy systems and manual processes, the current state of claims is on the brink of making or breaking insurers.
Here is how each of these key issues is impacting today’s claims experience:

Customers are demanding more personalized, seamless experiences across every industry — and insurance is no exception. When it comes to submitting a claim and tracking its status, policyholders expect a modern, omnichannel claims experience that balances digital elements with human interactions.

In addition, many prefer a self-service experience, with19% of insurance customers churningdue to a lack of self-service options. Consumers want transparent, real-time communication throughout the entire process, as well as greater visibility into the status of their claims.
Unfortunately, many insurers are still struggling to deliver this level of service, relying on outdated systems and manual processes that slow down resolution times and frustrate customers.
In addition to heightened customer expectations, the complexity of claims has increased significantly in recent years.

The rise in natural disasters and large-scale catastrophes has led to a surge in claims volume, often requiring more intricate handling and longer processing times. Swiss RE found total insured losses from natural disasters climbedpast $122 billion worldwide. On top of this, claims fraud is becoming increasingly sophisticated, leading to a higher frequency of fraudulent claims and greater scrutiny in processing each case. The propensity for litigation in claims has also increased, making claims management more complex than ever.
This complexity translates to longer cycle times, higher payouts, and more claims leakage, further eroding insurers’ profitability and consumers’ trust.

Another critical issue is the prevalence of outdated claims processes and legacy systems. While many insurers have upgraded their platforms, the underlying practices remain rooted in old, manual ways of doing things.

For example, although claims handling is done on newer platforms, it still requires human intervention at every step of the process. Even in cases where digital platforms are used, the processes themselves may not have been updated, or there is a lack of integration between systems, resulting in inefficiency and errors. This combination of outdated processes and systems leads to higher costs, delays, and missed opportunities for improvement. As a result, insurers face mounting pressure to modernize their claims operations to keep up with the evolving landscape.
These factors all make it harder — and make it take longer — to resolve claims, ultimately affecting customer satisfaction and insurers’ bottom lines.
While many insurers have taken steps to upgrade their platforms, there’s still much work to be done to truly transform internal operations and customer interactions.
Here are three key strategies to drive meaningful change in the claims landscape.

While many insurers have made strides by upgrading their claims management platforms, they still rely on outdated processes for claims handling, communication, and data sharing. Manual workflows create inefficiencies, delay resolutions, and negatively impact customer satisfaction.

To remain competitive, insurers must go beyond upgrading technology platforms — they need to redefine and transform their underlying processes. This means streamlining internal workflows, automating routine tasks, and enhancing the customer journey from claim submission to payout.

By improving both internal operations and customer-facing touchpoints, insurers can reduce costs, accelerate claims processing, and deliver a seamless, frictionless experience that meets evolving customer expectations.

Insurers who fail to leverage emerging technologies and new ecosystems risk being left behind. The rise of technologies like artificial intelligence (AI),generative AI (GenAI), machine learning, and IoT is reshaping the way claims can be processed and managed. Insurers have a significant opportunity to use these technologies to innovate and stay ahead.

In addition, insurtech companies and ecosystems specializing in specific claims processes — such as fraud detection, straight-through processing, low-touch claims, and document processing — offer valuable opportunities for integration. Partnering with organizations who can help insurers integrate these ecosystems and emerging technologies into their claims landscape can unlock efficiencies, reduce manual effort, and increase overall value.

For example, AI can be used to assess claims more accurately and quickly, while IoT devices can provide real-time data to help prevent claims from occurring in the first place. By embracing these technologies, insurers can streamline their processes, reduce fraud, and improve the overall claims experience for customers.

Behind every successful claim process, there are skilled claims adjusters who handle complex cases and engage directly with customers. However, many insurers are facing a growing skills gap as experienced adjusters retire and younger professionals enter the workforce. Protecting institutional knowledge and ensuring that new adjusters are equipped with the right skills is crucial for maintaining the quality of claims handling.

Insurers should focus on continuous training and development programs that equip adjusters with advanced communication, data analysis, and customer engagement skills. By transforming the role of adjusters from process-oriented operators to customer-focused advisors, insurers can not only improve the claims experience but also foster long-term customer loyalty.

As customer expectations continue to rise and claims grow more complex, the future of insurance claims depends on the seamless integration of technology, process optimization, and people transformation. Insurers have an opportunity to move beyond incremental improvements and create a transformative impact by reimagining the role of their claims departments.

By modernizing experiences, adopting cutting-edge technologies, and strategically investing in talent, insurers can significantly improve operational efficiency, enhance customer trust, and foster loyalty. More importantly, they can shift their claims function from being a reactive back-office cost center to a proactive, value-generating powerhouse.

The time to act is now. Insurers that adopt these strategies will not only redefine the claims experience but also position themselves as leaders in shaping the future of the industry. A well-executed transformation can make claims a competitive advantage, unlocking new levels of customer satisfaction and long-term profitability.
Interested in learning more about how to improve the customer experience? Read our case study, “Multi-line Insurer Improves Customer Experience with SmartCOMM.”

Why Transforming Claims Is Imperative
Raghavendra "Raghu" Aithal
SVP, Claims
ValueMomentum
Related Tags
Claims
Share this post
Subscribe to our newsletter
The insurance industry is at a crossroads when it comes to managing claims. A staggering 80 cents of every dollar earned on premiums is typically funneled into claims, which highlights the growing pressure insurers face to improve their claims processes. But cost isn’t the only reason insurers should prioritize transforming their claims operations: The
claims experience
remains a vital touchpoint between insurers and their customers.
Unfortunately, it’s also the source of the majority of consumer complaints in the industry,
70.9%, in fact
, reflecting a significant opportunity for improvement. Claims management is one of the most important levers for insurers to generate value and strengthen customer relationships. As the insurance ecosystem continues to evolve, transforming the claims value chain is no longer optional — it’s imperative for staying competitive.
The Current State of Claims
The insurance industry is grappling with a growing disconnect between customer expectations and
the current state of claims
management. Between the need for more digital experiences, growing threats within the insurance industry, and a reliance on legacy systems and manual processes, the current state of claims is on the brink of making or breaking insurers.
Here is how each of these key issues is impacting today’s claims experience:
Increased Expectations for Customer Experience
Customers are demanding more personalized, seamless experiences across every industry — and insurance is no exception. When it comes to submitting a claim and tracking its status, policyholders expect a modern, omnichannel claims experience that balances digital elements with human interactions.
In addition, many prefer a self-service experience, with
19% of insurance customers churning
due to a lack of self-service options. Consumers want transparent, real-time communication throughout the entire process, as well as greater visibility into the status of their claims.
Unfortunately, many insurers are still struggling to deliver this level of service, relying on outdated systems and manual processes that slow down resolution times and frustrate customers.
Increased Complexity in Claims
In addition to heightened customer expectations, the complexity of claims has increased significantly in recent years.
The rise in natural disasters and large-scale catastrophes has led to a surge in claims volume, often requiring more intricate handling and longer processing times. Swiss RE found total insured losses from natural disasters climbed
past $122 billion worldwide
. On top of this, claims fraud is becoming increasingly sophisticated, leading to a higher frequency of fraudulent claims and greater scrutiny in processing each case. The propensity for litigation in claims has also increased, making claims management more complex than ever.
This complexity translates to longer cycle times, higher payouts, and more claims leakage, further eroding insurers’ profitability and consumers’ trust.
Outdated Processes and Legacy Systems
Another critical issue is the prevalence of outdated claims processes and legacy systems. While many insurers have upgraded their platforms, the underlying practices remain rooted in old, manual ways of doing things.
For example, although claims handling is done on newer platforms, it still requires human intervention at every step of the process. Even in cases where digital platforms are used, the processes themselves may not have been updated, or there is a lack of integration between systems, resulting in inefficiency and errors. This combination of outdated processes and systems leads to higher costs, delays, and missed opportunities for improvement. As a result, insurers face mounting pressure to modernize their claims operations to keep up with the evolving landscape.
These factors all make it harder — and make it take longer — to resolve claims, ultimately affecting customer satisfaction and insurers’ bottom lines.
Transforming Insurance Claims: Three Strategic Imperatives for Insurers
While many insurers have taken steps to upgrade their platforms, there’s still much work to be done to truly transform internal operations and customer interactions.
Here are three key strategies to drive meaningful change in the claims landscape.
1. Modernize Internal and External Experiences
While many insurers have made strides by upgrading their claims management platforms, they still rely on outdated processes for claims handling, communication, and data sharing. Manual workflows create inefficiencies, delay resolutions, and negatively impact customer satisfaction.
To remain competitive, insurers must go beyond upgrading technology platforms — they need to redefine and transform their underlying processes. This means streamlining internal workflows, automating routine tasks, and enhancing the customer journey from claim submission to payout.
By improving both internal operations and customer-facing touchpoints, insurers can reduce costs, accelerate claims processing, and deliver a seamless, frictionless experience that meets evolving customer expectations.
2. Embrace Emerging Technologies and Ecosystems
Insurers who fail to leverage emerging technologies and new ecosystems risk being left behind. The rise of technologies like artificial intelligence (AI),
generative AI (GenAI)
, machine learning, and IoT is reshaping the way claims can be processed and managed. Insurers have a significant opportunity to use these technologies to innovate and stay ahead.
In addition, insurtech companies and ecosystems specializing in specific claims processes — such as fraud detection, straight-through processing, low-touch claims, and document processing — offer valuable opportunities for integration. Partnering with organizations who can help insurers integrate these ecosystems and emerging technologies into their claims landscape can unlock efficiencies, reduce manual effort, and increase overall value.
For example, AI can be used to assess claims more accurately and quickly, while IoT devices can provide real-time data to help prevent claims from occurring in the first place. By embracing these technologies, insurers can streamline their processes, reduce fraud, and improve the overall claims experience for customers.
3. Focus on People Transformation
Behind every successful claim process, there are skilled claims adjusters who handle complex cases and engage directly with customers. However, many insurers are facing a growing skills gap as experienced adjusters retire and younger professionals enter the workforce. Protecting institutional knowledge and ensuring that new adjusters are equipped with the right skills is crucial for maintaining the quality of claims handling.
Insurers should focus on continuous training and development programs that equip adjusters with advanced communication, data analysis, and customer engagement skills. By transforming the role of adjusters from process-oriented operators to customer-focused advisors, insurers can not only improve the claims experience but also foster long-term customer loyalty.
Driving the Future of Claims
As customer expectations continue to rise and claims grow more complex, the future of insurance claims depends on the seamless integration of technology, process optimization, and people transformation. Insurers have an opportunity to move beyond incremental improvements and create a transformative impact by reimagining the role of their claims departments.
By modernizing experiences, adopting cutting-edge technologies, and strategically investing in talent, insurers can significantly improve operational efficiency, enhance customer trust, and foster loyalty. More importantly, they can shift their claims function from being a reactive back-office cost center to a proactive, value-generating powerhouse.
The time to act is now. Insurers that adopt these strategies will not only redefine the claims experience but also position themselves as leaders in shaping the future of the industry. A well-executed transformation can make claims a competitive advantage, unlocking new levels of customer satisfaction and long-term profitability.

Product content management has historically been heavily manual, but these approaches can’t stay ahead of today’s changing market. A standardized approach can help insurers make product changes faster, reduce costs and errors, and improve regulatory compliance.
Commercial LinesProduct

Most commercial carriers manage their product content manually. Their product teams have to interpret large standard content manuals, track frequent circular updates, and translate that content into everything from rating logic to coverage and rules definitions and forms across multiple states and product lines. But manual approaches to aligning with industry-standard content cannot keep up with how fast things change.

According toRegEd, state-level insurance regulatory changes were already up more than 13% through mid-2025 compared to the same period in 2024 — and federal actions are expected to accelerate further, cascading additional requirements down to states. Across the industry, interpretation varies across products, teams, and states; updates are deferred; and workarounds accumulate.

A streamlined approach to insurance policy content management addresses each of these pressure points, enabling carriers to launch and update products faster, automate complex rating and compliance logic, and simplify maintenance across states and markets.
While product teams are aware of the need to update industry content as regulations change or new circulars are released, many have not implemented a standardized approach.
Here are six ways that manual product content management processes are creating friction in the day-to-day work of product teams:

Circulars are frequently deferred due to overlapping business priorities, leaving many carriers operating multiple update cycles behind current bureau content. Missed or delayed regulatory adoption increases audit findings, regulatory fines, corrective action plans, and state Department of Insurance scrutiny. It can also make remediation effort greater and create reputational risk that is difficult to quantify until it surfaces during a market conduct exam.

Every standard content change triggers a cascade of manual work: reconfiguring coverages, updating rules, revising forms, and validating rating logic, followed by extensive regression testing before anything reaches production. This leads to longer release cycles, higher defect rates, and slower speed to market when expanding into new states or launching new products.

Actuarial and IT teams in most commercial lines organizations spend a disproportionate amount of time on maintenance instead of on strategic activities. Advanced pricing analysis, portfolio optimization, and modernization initiatives all take a back seat to keeping existing products current, leaving carriers slower to adapt at precisely the moment the market demands more agility.

Manual product content management introduces misalignment between rating logic, underwriting rules, and policy forms, which only gets worse over time. The downstream consequences range from incorrect premiums, outdated policy forms, and coverage gaps to increased disputes, leakage, and combined ratio volatility.

Non-standard product definitions create friction at every regulatory checkpoint. Manual reconciliation is required to meet reporting standards, and the effort involved increases with each deviation introduced into the product model. This causes increased scrutiny during market conduct exams, additional audit and correction cycles, and a reactive compliance posture.

Product configuration, compliance testing, and regulatory filing are typically owned by different teams, with no single point of accountability. Decisions move slowly. Rework is common. And when something goes wrong, identifying where the breakdown occurred — and who is responsible for fixing it — takes longer than it should.

Individually, each of these challenges is manageable. But combined, they take up an increasing share of organizational capacity, leaving carriers less prepared for the evolving regulatory environment and less agile to adapt to market opportunities.

These pain points are the byproduct of a product content management process that was built for a lower volume and slower pace of regulatory change. A streamlined approach enables carriers to launch new products and roll out updates significantly faster — reducing the manual interpretation and configuration work that currently stretches release cycles.

Analysis of rating, forms, pricing, and compliance changes as well as the impact on the current portfolio can be streamlined with automation, along with the IT effort involved in these changes. Maintenance across products, states, and markets becomes simpler and more repeatable, and regulatory changes can be absorbed as routine rather than as a disruption to ongoing operations.

And the benefits of a streamlined approach extend across the organization. Product and underwriting teams can keep products standardized and up to date without constant rework. Actuarial and pricing teams can recover capacity consumed by manual circular analysis and regression testing and redirect their bandwidth to advanced pricing work and portfolio optimization. Compliance and regulatory teams gain the end-to-end traceability that market conduct exams demand.

Enabling a governed, repeatable model for product content management turns regulatory updates into an ongoing operational discipline, ensuring that carriers can evolve their product portfolio with the speed needed to stay ahead in a competitive landscape. This goes for rolling out new lines of business or expanding into additional regions with differing product requirements.

The regulatory environment commercial lines carriers are dealing with is not static, and the operational consequences of managing product content manually are becoming harder to absorb. As compliance gaps widen and the competitive need for product innovation and state expansion grows, a scalable, governed process for product content management is an investment in business agility.

Effective product content management is not merely a technology problem. It is an operational discipline that requires clear ownership, repeatable processes, and an infrastructure that keeps up with an increasingly complex regulatory environment.

paragraphs: HomeData & Advanced AnalyticsAugmented Claims Intelligence
Augmented Claims Intelligence
Augment claims handling and processing with a better understanding of your claims life cycle.

Our Augmented Claims Intelligence services help insurers optimize their claims workflows, assess claims severity and litigation propensity, and estimate losses by identifying trends and uncovering hidden insights in historical data.
How we help
Claims Performance Insights​
Enable context-aware Q&A and insights by leveraging LLMs and embeddings to reduce time to insight and empower adjusters with ad hoc business queries.
FNOL Outlier Detection
Identify anomalies in FNOL submissions by comparing incident details with historical claim behavior to flag fraud, accelerate clean claims, and auto-summarize reports.
Claim Complexity Segmentation
Classify claims into severity buckets using regression and natural language processing to allocate expert resources up front and prioritize high-value claims.
Matching Claims to the Right Adjuster
Route claims to the most suitable adjuster using graph-based assignment and decision trees to reduce rework and improve first-time-right resolution.
Adjuster Knowledge Management​
Leverage LLM-powered search and Q&A to provide adjusters with cross-organizational insights.
Settlement Optimization
Predict and prescribe optimal settlement strategies using medical, cost, and jurisdictional data to minimize indemnity leakage and litigation exposure.
Litigation Propensity Prediction and Attorney Selection​

Score claims based on the likelihood of attorney involvement to enable early negotiation and specialized adjuster routing, reducing legal costs and cycle times, as well as recommend the best-fit attorney for litigation based on case complexity, jurisdiction, and performance.
Early Subrogation Detection​
Detect subrogation opportunities at FNOL by analyzing liability, police, and third-party data to increase recovery rates and shorten timelines.
Fraud Complexity Scoring
Generate fraud risk scores at FNOL using link analysis and machine learning scoring to flag recycled photos, geolocation mismatches, and other fraud indicators early.

Customer Experience and Engagement
Personalize engagement, digital innovation, and seamless service experiences.

ValueMomentum enables insurers to deliver a more seamless, engaging experience that increases customer satisfaction, reduces churn, and drives long-term loyalty. Our solutions are designed to modernize and optimize customer service, improving both operational efficiency and the customer experience.
How we help
Customer Journey Mapping
We help insurers identify key moments of truth and build a customer journey that reduces friction and delights customers, enhancing overall customer experience.
Digital Transformation
Drawing from our domain knowledge and technology expertise, we advise insurers on how to leverage digital channels and technologies to modernize and enhance customer engagement.
Personalized Strategies
ValueMomentum leverages customer data and insights to help insurers tailor offerings and services and build deeper and more meaningful relationships with their customers.

Risk Management.
Proactively manage risk and ensure business continuity and compliance.

In an industry where risk is central, proactive risk management is essential. ValueMomentum helps insurers assess their risk exposure across all aspects of operations and implement strategies to minimize and mitigate those risks effectively.
How we help
Risk Assessment and Mitigation

Our risk assessment and mitigation services provide in-depth analysis and actionable recommendations to identify potential risks, from underwriting to regulatory compliance, and develop strategies to minimize exposure and protect your business.
Compliance and Regulatory Advisory

We provide expert advisory on compliance and regulatory issues, ensuring your business stays aligned with industry regulations. Our services include identifying compliance gaps, recommending solutions, and implementing frameworks to mitigate regulatory risks.

Strategy Consulting.
Empowering insurers with strategic insights and innovative solutions.

ValueMomentum helps insurers understand market dynamics and opportunities, advising on growth strategies, crafting innovative product offerings, and adapting business models to remain competitive. Our experienced consultants align strategy with both current market conditions and future trends, enabling insurers to capitalize on emerging opportunities while minimizing risks.
How we help
Market Entry and Growth Strategy

Our market entry and growth strategy services guide insurers on how to enter new territories or grow within established markets. By analyzing regional market trends, competitor landscapes, and customer needs, we deliver insights that drive market expansion and business scaling.
Product Development

We assist in the development of new insurance products or the enhancement of existing ones. From ideation to go-to-market strategies, ValueMomentum helps insurers create solutions that meet the needs of today’s customers while maximizing market impact.
Business Model Innovation

Our business model innovation services enable insurers to rethink how they operate and deliver value. By aligning your business model with industry disruptions and emerging technologies, we help insurers create agile, sustainable frameworks for long-term success.

Application Services.
Build scalable, future-ready applications to drive seamless digital transformation.

ValueMomentum’s application infrastructure solutions enable insurers to rapidly innovate, adapt, and scale in a competitive landscape. Our tailored solutions merge innovative frameworks with proven domain expertise to deliver robust applications that meet today’s business demands and anticipate tomorrow’s.
How we help
Application Development

We assist insurers with cloud-native development, seamless integration, and application modernization solutions, combining advanced frameworks and industry expertise to deliver resilient, scalable applications.
Application Re-Engineering

Our re-engineering services modernize legacy applications by transforming them into modern, scalable, microservices-based solutions that empower businesses to innovate, scale, and thrive in a digital-first world.
Integration

ValueMomentum’s integration solutions leverage APIs and microservices to seamlessly connect applications, enabling data flow, improved functionality, and streamlined workflows across your technology ecosystem.
API Strategy & Enablement

Define, design, and implement enterprise-grade API capabilities through a structured life cycle. Ourcomprehensive adoption approach leverages accelerators and scalable frameworks toimprove time to market, enhance governance, and drive savings.
Integration Platform

Enhance efficiency and accelerate delivery with a well-architected API platform that bridges the gap between the many distribution channels and data sources insurers use and their organization’s core systems and data.
App Development & Modernization

Drive more efficient development and modernization of your application architecture with our GenAI-fueledengineering frameworks for core, front-end, and cloud-native applications, with foundational aspects like data rationalization and context building embedded in the process.

Quality Assurance.
Drive excellence and resilience with comprehensive quality assurance solutions

With extensive experience in quality assurance, ValueMomentum delivers solutions that empower insurers to maintain high standards, reduce risk, and improve operational performance. Our tailored quality engineering services address core challenges, helping insurers enhance system reliability, security, and scalability.
How we help
AI-Driven Quality Engineering

Our GenAI-enabled test life-cycle automation solutions redefine efficiency, automating test creation, execution, and maintenance across UI, API, and data layers. Designed for the unique demands of P&C insurers, our solutions deliver faster, smarter, and adaptive testing while minimizing manual intervention and enhancing system reliability.
End-to-End Automation

Tailored specifically for the P&C insurance domain, our automation solutions help carriers streamline and scale their testing efforts across UI, API, and data layers to provide an efficient, reliable approach to testing that reduces manual effort. By centering automation, we enable P&C insurers to accelerate delivery timelines while maintaining the highest quality standards.
Performance Engineering for Exceptional User Experiences

We focus on optimizing system performance to ensure applications provide insurance stakeholders with reliable and responsive interactions, even in complex and dynamic environments. Through comprehensive testing and analysis, we help insurers maintain consistent performance and a smooth, efficient experience from quoting to claims processing.
Business Assurance

ValueMomentum’s business assurance services focus on the unique needs of P&C insurers, ensuring compliance; mitigating risks; and delivering reliable, industry-aligned solutions that support growth and operational goals.
Test Data Management
Implement robust test data management (TDM) governance and processes to deliver quality data seamlessly and help teamsensure the highest quality for enterprise testing.
Intelligent Automation

Streamline the entire testing process, from requirements analysis to defect logging to ongoing test case maintenance, by infusing the entire testing life cycle with machine-learning-driven automation.
NextGen Quality Engineering

Build quality into the fabric of your enterprise with a continuous quality orchestration approachthat spans an organization’s AI systems, connected devices, and platforms and leverages P&C-specific accelerators and build-in governance measures.

title: Acuity Automates Customer Correspondence with CCM Platform
meta_description: Want to streamline and centralize customer communications across the entire enterprise? Here's how Acuity Insurance did it with a new CCM platform.

headings.text: Acuity Automates Customer Correspondence with CCM Platform
Global Specialty Insurer Streamlines CCM Platform

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, USA
Saved significant business user and IT time and resources with the rationalization of forms
Enhanced business user satisfaction with the implementation of a new CCM platform
Addressed the compliance issue efficiently by rapid migration of forms
Developed an internal team and prepared them with the needed technical skills and knowledge to support enterprise forms migration
Core Platforms

Founded in 1925, Acuity Insurance, a mutual insurance company, provides property and casualty insurance products for consumers and businesses across 28 states in the United States. As an organization, Acuity relentlessly focuses on innovative ways to improve efficiency an increase productivity in order to deliver high-quality products and servi to its customers and agents. Acuity insures over 125,000 businesses, including 325,000 commercial vehicles, and nearly half a million homes and private passenger autos. The company is headquartered in Sheboygan, Wisconsin.

Acuity relied largely on legacy technologies for their documentation needs; outdated technologies such as XICS and Microsoft Word were used for forms across various services, including applications, claims, audit, and loss control. The company was digitalizing documents manually which was a tedious task and prone to errors. Chris Lensmeyer, Director – Business Systems added, “These outdated technologies were non-compliant with the seamless customer correspondence experience that we wanted to provide.” With XICS support coming to an end, Acuity set out to look for a CCM platform in the market that would meet their growing needs for documents now and into the future.

With the goal of centralizing forms and enabling the delivery of personalized and multi-channel customer communications, Acuity decided to implement the OpenText Exstream CCM platform for its capabilities of enhancing one-to-one customer interactions and improving customer experience. For the herculean task of converting 7,000 forms within a reasonable timeframe, Acuity wanted to leverage the support of an IT services partner since it would require significant resources and technical expertise.

Acuity chose ValueMomentum as its IT services partner for its insurance domain experience and technical implementation expertise, specifically for the OpenText Exstream platform. With the help of ValueMomentum, Acuity built an enterprise-wide architecture to support the CCM platform. OpenText Exstream, including Empower and EWS running on the WebSphere application server, was integrated with Acuity’s home-grown applications and their existing forms portal. Over a 36-month period, a team of 35 resources consisting of project managers, developers, and business units—from Acuity IT staff, ValueMomentum, and OpenText—deployed the CCM platform on-premise. The deployment was done in three phases of over 12 months each: 1. creating a GUI, 2. integrating the platform, and 3. converting forms. Once deployed, an agile sprint framework was adopted for the migration of forms.

Speaking about the collaboration and execution of the project, Jim Glavan, General Manager – Information Technology stated, “ValueMomentum’s team exhibits a strong sense of ownership, and their technical expertise brought efficiency to the implementation as well as ensured high quality in the development of our forms.”

Implementing an enterprise CCM platform that integrated with Acuity’s core systems enabled them to automate their documentation process. The new intuitive, on-demand portal-based platform allowed Acuity to rationalize around 28% of total forms, remove 15% of forms that were redundant, and provide users access to the centralized repository of most up-to-date versions of forms. The automation also reduced forms maintenance resources by 65%. Other key productivity measures include 1,250 business and IT user hours saved in 2017 at the outset, with 9,000 IT hours and 70,000 business user hours projected to be saved by 2022. The modern OpenText Exstream platform enabled Acuity to save time spent on the conversion of forms by 50 percent. Moreover, the streamlined documentation process and consistency across forms helped Acuity to focus on critical business areas that will contribute to their business growth. Empower implementation enabled the end-users to submit the updated forms to the centralized print from anywhere. During the unprecedented times of COVID-19, it has been highly helpful to all the stakeholders with everyone working remotely.

Acuity attributed the success of this project to OpenText Exstream and Empower functionalities, effective collaboration between business units and ValueMomentum, and the focus on user training. On the partnership with ValueMomentum, Chris commented, “ValueMomentum is an integral part of Acuity’s team. I do not need to worry about any iterations required in our development and migration processes to suit the evolving customer needs. They take on any new requirements proactively.”

headings.text: Erie Insurance Optimizes Data Operations with MarkLogic Enterprise Data Hub on AWS
Driving Business Value with Insurance Data Analytics

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, United States
Modern cloud data platform and single source of truth for datadriven decision-making
Improved speed to market for new products, services, technologies, and geographies
Increased retention rates of households/businesses
Enhanced ability to adapt to new or changed regulations and risks to the business
Enabled ability to connect customers to new product categories for up-selling and cross-selling
Data

Erie Insurance (ERIE) is a Fortune 500 company with operations in 12 states and Washington, D.C. The company was founded in 1925 with a mission to emphasize service excellence above all else. It sells auto, home, commercial, and life insurance through a network of 13,000 independent agents and has 6M+ policies in force.

To modernize insurance policy processes and enhance its reporting and analytics capabilities, Erie Insurance had built a centralized onpremises data hub, powered by the Progress MarkLogic Data Hub (DH).

After years of use, ERIE needed to enhance its MarkLogic DH implementation to increase storage and enable the ability to quickly spin up new environments or proof-of-concept clusters to provide more responsive support and growth options for the enterprise. The company decided to migrate to MarkLogic on Amazon Web Services (AWS).
ERIE turned to its long-term partner, ValueMomentum — who was involved in the early stages of the implementation — to support the migration effort.

Moving its MarkLogic DH implementation to the cloud required ERIE to ensure the completeness and accuracy of the data migrated from legacy systems. Since ERIE had a wide variety of data sources, including structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data from both modern and legacy systems, this proved to be a challenge given their access methods, data quality, data governance, and complex business rules.

ERIE worked with ValueMomentum to design and develop the cloud environment, create data harmonization workflows, and test and deploy the application. As part of this project, data was extracted; transformed to fit a harmonized data model; and loaded into MarkLogic DH, a subject area mart (SAM), and an earned data mart (EDM), creating a unified view of policy details, coverages, endorsements, premiums, etc.

The Consolidated Data Source (CDS), a part of ERIE’s new Enterprise Data Hub, consolidated policy data from modern policy administration systems and soon after, ERIE’s legacy policy, billing, and claims systems as well. This consolidated data was made available for system-to-system interactions, search, advanced analytics and reporting, and more.

The Customer Information Management (CIM) system, another critical component of ERIE’s Enterprise Data Hub, consolidated customer data from policy administration and other systems, harmonizing it into a unified 360-degree and cross-portfolio view of each customer.

As the application moved into production, ValueMomentum provided ERIE with ongoing development, support, and maintenance, as well as system and workload updates, and enhancements to MarkLogic on AWS to support business needs.

MarkLogic DataHub on AWS provides a single source of truth for ERIE, enhancing operational efficiency, reducing data inconsistencies, and enabling better decision-making through improved analytics. It also provides insights into customer behavior, preferences, and risk profiles, informing strategies for marketing, product development, and pricing.

Underwriters, actuaries, product owners, and other business users can access CDS to search for policies, view policy details, and analyze policy performance metrics. CDS enables efficient policy-centric reporting and analysis, such as policy count reports, premium trend analysis, policy risk assessments, and earned premium reports. This supports use cases like identifying profitable policy segments, monitoring policy retention, and informing product pricing decisions.

CIM and CDS also enable ERIE to retire legacy systems, resulting in IT cost savings and a streamlined application landscape. These tools demonstrate the value of unified, reliable data platforms in driving operational efficiency, analytics-driven decision-making, and business transformation
Ultimately, migrating to MarkLogic on AWS fosters agility, data-driven decision-making, and operational efficiency, driving ERIE’s business success in a competitive landscape.

meta_description: To drive better user experience for adjusters and claimants, cut down on the time and cost required to generate claims documents, and drive overall operational efficiency, a Fortune 500 insurer decided to modernize its claims content management process.

headings.text: Fortune 500 Insurer Improves Efficiency and Experience With Claims Correspondence Modernization
Fortune 500 Insurer Elevates Customer Experience with New CCM Platform
Regional Carrier Revitalizes Claims Organization With Cloud-Native Platform

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, United States
Reduced claims letter cycle time from around four days to under three hours
Lowered IT input required for customized letters
Cut operational costs associated with claims letters
With additional digital capabilities on the roadmap, slated to drive up to $1 million annual savings
ClaimsFeatured
The client is a Fortune 500 company that sells auto, home,commercial, and life insurance.

A Fortune 500 insurer sought to improve its content management and production capabilities to deliver a better adjuster and claimant experience, enhance the efficiency of its claims document processes, and greatly reduce costs associated with claims documents. Its claims letter program did not provide enough flexibility for the insurer’s claims handlers to create customized letters and route them for approval, resulting in an average document processing time of around four days. These rigid and time-intensive processes made business users heavily reliant on the IT team for any necessary changes or updates.

The insurer’s previous tech stack consisted of a legacy dictation processing system and a homegrown system that enabled the team to issue standard, template-based letters. In order to democratize customization capabilities and improve efficiency across its claims content processes, the carrier decided to implement a modern content solution that could integrate smoothly with its newly implemented primary claims solution.

Leveraging a modern platform would allow business users to make letter updates without IT involvement while still providing a controlled environment that ensured messaging was consistent and compliant across the organization. In addition to this factory concept, which eased the maintenance of document templates and improved efficiency, the insurer wanted to enable electronic signature and notarization of documents as well as to automate e-delivery options, status tracking, and the approvals process.

As a long-time strategic partner to the insurer, ValueMomentum was involved in all phases of the project, from business analysis to development to quality assurance (QA). The team worked to identify the platforms that would deliver the experience and efficiencies the carrier’s claims organization was looking for.

ValueMomentum conducted a demo on the new CCM tool features and implemented a proof of concept to determine the feasibility of the tool meeting the insurer’s business needs and integrating with the claims system’s front end.

Core Platforms

Since 1947, Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho has provided a full range of insurance products to families, farms, and businesses. The largest property and casualty insurer headquartered in Idaho, it expanded into Washington in 2023 as Western Community Insurance Company, holds an A (Excellent) AM Best rating, and is a 2025 Best Place to Work in Idaho honoree.

Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho knew that to remain competitive in the market, it needed to streamline system upgrades and be able to more rapidly bring enhancements and new products to market. To achieve this goal, the insurer decided to modernize its on-premises InsuranceSuite instance by migrating to GWCP.

By upgrading to GWCP, Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho aimed to harness the power of cloud, seamlessly adopt the platform’s latest innovations via the SaaS solution, modernize its core systems to enable better agility, and provide a more modern user experience for internal and external stakeholders. Quickly achieving these benefits was important to the insurer, so the team stewarding the complex project devised an ambitious timeline of 12 months from inception to go-live.

Having worked with ValueMomentum on other projects, Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho knew that not only did ValueMomentum have a keen understanding of its business goals and the processes powering the property and casualty insurance life cycle, but also, as a Guidewire Consulting partner at the Select level, it had the technical expertise and knowledge of Guidewire systems required for the project.

ValueMomentum, with a team of around 40 associates, worked proactively with Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho and Guidewire to ensure that the complexity of a cloud migration project did not interrupt the delivery of other company projects.

The teams worked across four structured phases: a one-month inception and analysis phase, a six-month period of development, nearly two months of complete regression testing and retrofitting parallel program code, and a final three-month stabilization and go-live phase.

As with any core modernization effort, the teams had to navigate competing business priorities, technical hurdles, and a unique delivery strategy on top of multiple ongoing projects. Serving as the lead implementation partner, ValueMomentum oversaw program management as well as the requirements and development phases, integrations, and quality assurance.

Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho’s team led the project management office, architectural oversight, data solutions, and deployment coordination. After the successful migration of PolicyCenter, BillingCenter, ClaimCenter, and Contact Management to GWCP, ValueMomentum’s team led performance testing and asynchronous quote implementation and crafted a new approach for file mediation services.

“ValueMomentum brought commitment, expertise, and a one-team mindset — critical to delivering this program successfully,” said Shilynn Francisco, vice president of Information Systems at Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho. “On complex projects like this, hitting the target date is rare. ValueMomentum partnered with our team and Guidewire to deliver on time and achieve the results we were seeking.”

Thanks to collaboration across all of the teams involved, the project was successfully completed within the planned 12-month period. By migrating to GWCP, Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho projects a 40% increase in speed to market for new products. The migration has also simplified updates, enabling the insurer to quickly leverage new Guidewire capabilities and freeing up IT resources to focus on other strategic business initiatives.

“This modernization has strengthened our technology foundation so we can better support the communities we serve across Idaho and Washington,” Francisco said. “With Guidewire, we can adopt new capabilities with each release, keeping our products at the forefront of the industry and making our customers’ lives easier every day.”

Investing in a modern, cloud-based core platform has streamlined operational tasks like hardware maintenance, environment management, security patching, and testing. Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho has already seen a reduction in overhead expenses, better agility to respond to market changes, and accelerated upgrade time with reduced cost.

Insurance, United States

Improved customer experience

Core Platforms

Since 1947, Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho has provided a full range of insurance products to families, farms, and businesses. The largest property and casualty insurer headquartered in Idaho, it expanded into Washington in 2023 as Western Community Insurance Company, holds an A (Excellent) AM Best rating, and is a 2025 Best Place to Work in Idaho honoree.

In an effort to modernize and streamline its payment experience for policyholders and agents, Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho wanted to upgrade its aging payment platform, NEXUS, to a more agile platform that was integrated with its insurance core systems. The old platform was costly and provided limited functionality.

To bring customers a modern payment experience, Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho sought out an updated platform that offered a payment processing system, a payment status synchronizer, reporting functionality, notifications, and a messaging system to enable reliable messaging in a publishsubscribe integration model for future additions. After conducting a thorough search for a new platform, the insurer selected ACI Worldwide as its new payment system, largely due to its preexisting integration plug-ins with Guidewire Insurance Suite.

Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho wanted to develop a robust integration between its Guidewire core systems and the new payment system to ensure all payments were processed accurately. In addition, the insurer wanted the flexibility to waive or change fees as needed by making the logic behind the fees configurable. It was also important for payments to be allowed from multiple sources, including the insurer’s mobile app, its public website, the HUB website, and Guidewire PolicyCenter and BillingCenter.

When looking for a services partner to help it successfully decommission its old payment system and integrate the new one, Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho turned to its existing partner, ValueMomentum. Having successfully completed another project with the organization, the insurer knew that ValueMomentum had the necessary insurance knowledge and technical expertise to successfully modernize its payment system.

ValueMomentum worked with internal stakeholders as well as the insurer’s project management office team across the development, testing, and implementation phases of the project. ValueMomentum’s team partnered with Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho to successfully manage the insurer’s business requirements and implement the Guidewire and integration code changes needed to seamlessly integrate with ACI’s system.

As part of the initiative, ValueMomentum was responsible for the end-to-end development process, including the design and execution of comprehensive testing to validate all of the integration requirements. In addition, ValueMomentum worked closely with ACI to coordinate the deployment of changes across multiple environments, culminating in a smooth rollout. The project was completed in just over one year, commencing in September 2023 and going live in November 2024.

The successful project has not only reduced operating costs associated with the payments process by 75%, but it has also yielded a modernized digital payment process for customers across all lines of business. For instance, the company can now leverage automation for applying payments and managing reversals, creating a more streamlined process for customers, agents, and employees.

Customers and agents are also seeing a better, more consistent user experience. The new payment platform is fully integrated with Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho’s Guidewire core systems and mobile app, enabling policyholders to access their information and make transactions when and where they want, including the ability to schedule future-dated payments.

For agents, the updated client console exhibits payments in a central dashboard, allowing agents to view both past and upcoming payments in one place. The platform has also laid the groundwork for the insurer to handle other payment methods and digital wallets such as Apple Pay, PayPal, or Google Wallet.

title: Fortune 500 Insurer Elevates Customer Experience with New CCM Platform

headings.text: Fortune 500 Insurer Elevates Customer Experience with New CCM Platform
Global Specialty Insurer Streamlines CCM Platform
Pekin Insurance Adopts Enterprise CCM for Automated Document Generation
Acuity Automates Customer Correspondence with CCM Platform

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, United States
Improved customer satisfaction via omnichannel communications and realtime documents access
Satisfied evolving customer and business demands
Simplified CCM system technology and architecture while reducing maintenance costs
Reduced batch processing errors and reliance on print and manual labor
Core Platforms

The Fortune 500 insurer offers auto, home, business, and life insurance through a network of independent insurance agents. The insurer has more than 6 million policies in force and operates in 12 states. It is among the 20 largest P&C insurers in the U.S.

Aiming to deepen relationships with customers, the Fortune 500 insurer recognized a lack of communication channels for customers to engage with agents. To adapt to changing expectations and support long-term growth, the Fortune 500 insurer wanted a digital-first CCM platform that would support omnichannel communications and suppress paper transactions.

The insurer’s end-to-end print process used more than 100 legacy components to deliver transactional documents using OpenText Exstream 16.4. It had been printing more than 250,000 invoices and other transactional documents daily.

The Fortune 500 insurer wanted to transition to an e-delivery invoice system, enabled through online accounts for customers. Modernization would allow it to provide digital access for customers and agents, improve its claims payment notifications and e-delivery systems, and standardize content authoring for letter generation.

ValueMomentum helped the Fortune 500 insurer build an enterprisewide architecture to support the CCM platform by developing the CCM components required for migration, then strategized to implement the solution across applications. ValueMomentum and the Fortune 500 insurer then migrated more than 140 forms across personal, commercial, claims, and billing portfolios.

In addition, ValueMomentum upgraded the insurer’s OpenText system to v 16.6. On the Exstream system, the team established a more elaborate notification system for claims payment, implemented business rules and orchestration for e-delivery, and created content authoring capabilities for letter generation.

While working toward fully digital communications, paper suppressions were first implemented for invoice applications, then declarations, ID cards, and other transactional documents. They implemented an email system to service existing applications and other communications while deploying the full CCM platform delivery infrastructure.

Operating on a contemporary CCM platform allows the Fortune 500 insurer to align with business and customer demands for digital-first communications through email, text, and voice notifications. It will be able to position itself as competitive with other customer-centric insurers and demonstrate how it is evolving to meet customer preferences.

The Fortune 500 insurer will be able to simplify its complicated legacy-dependent communications systems by transitioning to a CCM platform that streamlines operations while enabling future growth and scale. This will help to reduce batch processing errors and manual deployments steps, as well as decrease reliance on IT for custom-code changes.

By establishing a system of e-delivery of invoices through online accounts, the Fortune 500 insurer can leverage real-time availability of documents and increase point-of-services interactions to increase customer satisfaction during the claims process. The system also reduces manual labor, such as time spent searching for and providing documents for customers.

The client is a Fortune 500 company that sells auto, home, commercial, and life insurance.

The insurer’s previous subrogation identification process involved running predictive models independently of the claims system then transferring those results to claims supervisors. The insurer saw a major opportunity to reduce claims leakage, cut down on missed chances for subrogation, improve the efficiency of adjuster reviews, and ensure precision through real-time predictive insights. The claims and data teams were especially aware of how critical it was to integrate an enhanced subrogation model with its claims platform to achieve real-time data access and insights.

Having worked with its long-time strategic partner ValueMomentum on numerous other claims-related projects, the insurer chose to execute this project alongside ValueMomentum and core systems platform partners. The initiative required close collaboration between the business and IT across the 11-month timeline, from business analysis and development to integration and quality assurance (QA). The teams worked together in two-week sprints using an Agile Scrum process, which was a new way of working for the carrier.

The insurer’s claims team developed and deployed the subrogation model on cloud-based data modeling tools, then worked with ValueMomentum to integrate the machine learning model with its leading claims platform. On top of adjusting to the new way of working, integrating the machine learning model and platform with the claims system required heavy cross-collaboration across multiple internal and external teams. headings.text: Fortune 500 Insurer Revolutionizes Homeowners with AI and Aerial Imagery
How to Leverage AI in Insurance for Better Business Outcomes
AI in Software Testing: New Use Cases for Insurers

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, United States
$3.5M saved so far, exceeding the initial $2.5M estimate
Estimated benefit of re-underwriting 12,000 roofs in poor condition: $22M
Estimated benefit of re-underwriting undocumented pools: $5M annually
Data

The insurer is a Fortune 500 company with operations in 12 states and Washington, D.C. The company was founded in 1925 with a mission to emphasize service excellence above all else. It sells auto, home, commercial, and life insurance through a network of 13,000 independent agents and has 6M+ policies in force.
The insurer faced several challenges: high costs from roofing-related claims, as well as adverse selection against competitors already using aerial imagery in their underwriting process.

The insurer also faced the risk of customer dissatisfaction due to claims denied because of poor maintenance. It also found that it was subsidizing policyholders filing preventable claims, leading to higher rates. To address these issues, the insurer decided to identify properties with the worst roofs to be remedied or to cancel/non-renew the policies.

With help from ValueMomentum, the team rolled out an AI-model-driven system built on AWS. This modular framework utilizes Amazon Location Service and other third-party data to procure aerial imagery and location data. AI models then run a batch analysis. Factoring in roof condition and confidence scores, the system identifies roofs in poor condition to be remedied or to cancel/non-renew the policy. Reports are run monthly.

The solution also includes a Mendix-hosted UI for the underwriting team to inspect severe conditions remotely, mitigating the need for on-site visits. The technology is completely cloud native, and the deployment process was automated through CI/CD, achieving scalability and easy adaptations of future models.
Value was immediately realized, not just in cost savings but also in establishing a standardized, modern technology stack that improved both underwriting precision and customer satisfaction.

The integration of AI and aerial imagery in the insurer’s underwriting process is a technological triumph as well as a business case for thoughtful, cloud-native IT innovation aimed at critical industry challenges.

This endeavor resulted in immediate financial gains, with $3.5M saved annually — exceeding initial estimates of $2.5M. Moreover, the precise re-underwriting of 12,000 properties with poor roof conditions is projected to yield $22M, and identifying undocumented pools is expected to add another $5M in annual savings.

Beyond the financial metrics, the project has elevated the insurer’s competitive positioning in the market. As competitors were already leveraging similar technology, falling behind was not an option. The insurer’s modernization aligns it with industry best practices, effectively mitigating the risks of adverse selection, and premium losses.

Equally important is the boost in customer satisfaction. By proactively identifying maintenance issues, the company significantly reduces the instances of claim denials, thus improving the customer experience. This fusion of technology and strategy underscores that IT projects, at their core, are about enhancing the user experience for all stakeholders: customers, agents, brokers, and partners alike.

headings.text: Global P&C Insurer Drives Automation with OpenText Exstream & Guidewire PolicyCenter
NJM Grew Commercial Lines with Guidewire PolicyCenter Coverages

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, USA
Accelerated quote/proposal creation times for underwriters compared to the previous manual method
Improved adherence to compliance enabled by automated document generation workflows
Enabled faster and more effective signature process using the DocuSign integration capability
Core Platforms

The insurer provides reinsurance and insurance products globally. Within the reinsurance market specifically, this insurer offers extensive and customized solutions to their customers. This capacity derives from their focus on underwriting excellence, coupled with strong risk and capital management. This insurer takes pride in their underwriting strength, which allows them to efficiently tailor individual policies to provide the responsive service and customized products their customers seek.

Document generation—a critical part of underwriting—was a manual and time-consuming process at the company, with underwriters still using Microsoft Excel-based rating and generation tools. Given the disparate tools and systems environment—in which each line of business might use a different system—generating quote letters, binder letters and policy packets required underwriters to go back and forth between various systems. These manual interventions drained underwriters’ time and raised the likelihood of human error.

The insurer set out to implement Guidewire PolicyCenter and OpenText Exstream as their modern PAS and CCM platform to streamline the underwriting process, increase the efficiency of their underwriting staff, and ultimately grow the business. These platforms would serve both its reinsurance and insurance branches’ document automation processes. Since this plan was part of a larger project at the enterprise level, and involved an aggressive timeline of 7-8 month releases, the insurer recognized the need for a vendor partner that could help drive the implementation.

The carrier went through an informal RFP process with three vendors to determine their SI partner. Through this evaluation process and with the recommendation of OpenText, they selected ValueMomentum. Key to their decision were the technical skills and industry-specific expertise demonstrated by the ValueMomentum team.

ValueMomentum helped the insurer install Exstream, establish an enterprise-wide architecture to support the new CCM platform, and develop Exstream interactive documents that would meet their needs. As the provider aimed to leverage its new CCM platform across the enterprise, ValueMomentum ensured the architecture was set up to support automated document workflow for both insurance and reinsurance lines of business. As part of this project, Exstream Empower was integrated with Guidewire Underwriter Management and Guidewire PolicyCenter. The insurer also leveraged Empower to build out five specialty products and 1200+ interactive documents. In addition, the underwriter worksheet, Manu-scripting, and DocuSign were also developed in or integrated with Exstream to create a seamless underwriting experience.

Having an enterprise CCM platform connected to modern core systems allowed the P/C insurance provider to automate the entire underwriting process in one system. Typically, the process of quoting, binding, and issuing a policy would take the insurer 2-4 hours. With the new CCM platform, underwriters were able to complete the process in just 10 minutes. The increased efficiency allowed underwriters to close more proposals each day, thus contributing to an increase in total premiums and overall company revenue. The OpenText platform will also allow for DocuSign integration and facilitate electronic signatures in the future, which would have been impossible in their former environment.

By matching their aggressive timeline to implement Guidewire PolicyCenter and OpenText Exstream, the insurer has successfully built automation and straight-through processing into their underwriting procedure. These new capabilities promise significant time-saving and increased productivity for their underwriters, who can now drive more meaningful business value by focusing on underwriting instead of manual document generation.

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, United States
Reduced manual effort
Enhanced user experience

Centralized processes for data transfer
Core Platforms

A global specialist insurer with a branch in the U.S. that underwrites a diverse range of personal and commercial insurance risks. They focus on underserved needs and specialty commercial clients via both the regional broker and direct distribution channels, serving over 500,000 customers.

The insurer has experienced extremely rapid growth over the past 11 years. To further take advantage of opportunities in the US market, the company has set an ambitious goal to realize $1B in GWP and $100M in profit. To accomplish this goal, it’s critical that the insurer positions itself to capture market share by increasing its regulatory and operational robustness, driving efficiencies, and enabling high quality broker and customer experiences. The company’s legacy IT systems and dependent processes pose a major challenge to this goal.

As part of its communications systems, the insurer relies on a number of CCM systems for document generation. They use Magic and Oneshield as their policy administrative systems, to feed data to Thunderhead and SmartCOMM platforms, which then create forms and documents for customer communication. These documents are generated by Thunderhead and include Renewal Letter, Coverage Summary, Package (contains Declarations, Endorsements, Notices, Policy Wording & Statement of Fact), and Acord & Billing deals with different risks.

However, unstructured data inputted into the system resulted in batch failures across these information sets. Because the final document must intake all data, failure in a single transaction would lead to issues in the entire batch. Thus, the application and maintenance (AMS) team needed to exert a significant amount of manual effort to manage errors, investigate and reprocess business users’ incident reports. The manual process was also error prone and time consuming. The insurer needed an easy-to-maintain solution that would address data transfer and batch failure while reducing complications to optimize the document generation process as well as improve the experience for its customers.

ValueMomentum has supported the insurer in their management of its CCM systems and understands the technical and business environment of the company. For this reason, the insurer decided to partner with VM for the enhancement and development of their CCM platforms to support the growth of their business.

A major initiative from the insurer aimed to replace aging systems and leverage the opportunity to simplify, accelerate and unlock new ways to further the company’s competitive advantage. As part of this initiative, the insurer optimized the generation of 13M+ documents from Thunderhead and Smart Communications to improve customer communications for various insurance products, such as General Liability, Professional Liability, Business Owners Policy & Cyber LOBs across all states for Direct, Partner Lines (DPD), and Broker Channels. ValueMomentum helped migrate documents from hybrid cloud into Pure Cloud AWS Platform to improve services and efficiency and shift spending away from servers and other onpremises legacy systems and technology.

The insurer worked with VM to identify any critical issues associated with batch failures, external images, and data and find solutions for the root cause of the issues. To ensure that documents were compliant and up to date, VM updated addresses for 260+ documents, updated logos on communication forms for partners, and executed change request and minor enhancements. VM also developed forms for new lines of business and new state roll outs and managed the integration of SmartComm with OneShield and Webmethods platforms to streamline end-to-end business processes associated with policy, billing and claims. With the resources and skills from VM’s CCM team, the insurer was able to improve document generation and enhance customer experience to support its business priorities.

Leveraging VM for the management and development of its CCM platforms, the insurer was able to eliminate issues associated with batch failures and data inputted into the system. As a result, the insurer significantly reduced manual effort spent on addressing every PROD batch failure and production incident.

The project also created a centralized solution for the redundant issue with reusable component which helps to accommodate changes to endorsement documents for print. This approach further reduced post-processing time and the manual labor of printing and mailing the documents. Moreover, the streamlined documentation process and consistency across forms helped the insurer to focus on critical business areas that will contribute to its business growth.

The migration of forms to the Pure Cloud AWS platform enabled scale and elasticity—allowing the insurer to dynamically scale to peak volume needs—and provided real-time access to the latest and most secure features without the lengthy upgrade cycles. With the technical and domain expertise of the VM team managing the CCM platforms and document generation, the insurer is able to focus on rolling out products and capture market opportunities.

Increased business agility

FeaturedQuality Engineering

Hiscox protects more than 600,000 small business customers of all types across the US, offering coverage ranging from  short-term liability to cybersecurity and more. It is part of the  Hiscox Group, an international specialist insurer that has been in operation since 1901 and serves customers in 13 countries.

Hiscox wanted to revitalize its approach to testing and quality engineering (QE) to deliver quality across every phase of the software development life cycle (SDLC) rather than sticking with the traditional, siloed configuration of its existing QE department. The insurer knew that turning QE into more of a partner than a separate function that joins at the tail end of the SDLC would provide a better balance between speed and safety, more consistent outcomes across all lines of business, and significant efficiency and cost savings.

Initial goals for the effort were to better understand what gaps existed and where they were to enable faster speed to market for enhancements and new products across professional liability (PL), general liability (GL), cyber, and businessowners (BOP) lines of business. Hiscox leadership wanted to become equipped for truly data-driven decision-making, surfacing information during performance testing to help solve issues before they made it to production.

The insurer decided that the key to a more consistent delivery process with higher quality from the outset was to improve its organizational approach to QE and quality assurance alongside its cloud deployment. It was also critical to offer a modern, responsive experience that provided the right information at the right time to stakeholders ranging from employees and agents to partners and retail customers.

ValueMomentum has partnered with Hiscox in a development and application support capacity for several years. When the insurer began its large-scale investment into its QE overhaul, ValueMomentum was brought on board to double-check  application support. This expanded into development work and testing services before becoming a full managed services partner. To truly reinvent Hiscox’s QE approach, the insurer and ValueMomentum prioritized three key elements: automating as much as possible, setting up a Test Center of Excellence (TCoE), and bringing testing earlier into the SDLC.

The ValueMomentum team worked closely with Hiscox and OneShield to drive a scalable enterprise QE (EQE) approach alongside the insurer’s cloud migration efforts.  ValueMomentum developed a metrics-driven TCoE to help  establish and uphold best practices across testing and  application maintenance, as well as some development  support. As part of the EQE and TCoE initiative, ValueMomentum helped implement Automate First, a program that trains testers to automate tests rather than creating each individual test manually, and instituted a shift-left approach, testing earlier and more often rather than relying on pre-go-live regression testing.

Revamping its approach to EQE helped Hiscox discover the root cause of existing issues it was facing, such as with rating. To optimize this critical process, ValueMomentum worked with Hiscox to develop a custom rating validation engine that confirms rate changes are applied correctly, more effectively, and in less time.

Transforming QE from a late-stage function into a partner that is involved across the entire SDLC enabled Hiscox to shrink its time to market while improving leakage. In addition, the program brought regression testing down from five days to two days. For specific fixes enabled by the EQE and TCoE efforts, such as the more accurate and efficient approach to rating validation, Hiscox has already seen cost savings, with a projected added revenue of more than $1M in the first year since deployment.

With strong EQE in place and a dedicated TCoE established, Hiscox has built business agility into its foundation, enabling it to provide employees with better tools and policyholders and partners with a seamless and defect-free experience. In addition, the more comprehensive approach to EQE and testing has shifted the culture within Hiscox, turning QE into a partner rather than a silo and setting the stage for faster, more effective innovation.
