Accelerated speed to market for new products and enhancements
Accelerated quoting process
Built a platform to drive better user experience for policyholders and agents
Core Platforms

Based out of Cheshire, Connecticut, HAI Group is the leading property and casualty insurer founded by and dedicated to supporting providers of public and affordable housing. Active for nearly 40 years, its team serves more than 1,800 housing organizations across the United States, offering insurance, risk management services, housing-focused training, and housing industry research.

Since its inception, HAI Group had been operating on a homegrown core platform. While this legacy system served the insurer well for many years, as the organization grew, its technology wasn’t adapting to the evolving needs of the business

HAI Group decided that it needed to modernize its core systems to serve customers better, respond to market changes more effectively, and bring new products and enhancements to market faster. HAI Group’s leadership team devised a five-year modernization plan, starting with a data warehouse modernization project to keep business running seamlessly, even while undergoing a core systems transformation.

Since the legacy system handled not just policy administration but also claims and billing, the insurer was seeking a core platform that could handle all of these functions. HAI Group knew that quality assurance (QA) would play an integral role in the core transformation project. Along with selecting a modern core platform, the insurer prioritized identifying a QA services partner that had deep insurance industry knowledge, QA expertise, and technical experience in the chosen platform.

After a thorough assessment phase, including a targeted demo phase and a questionnaire developed with heavy involvement from internal business stakeholders, HAI Group selected OneShield as its new core system provider and GhostDraft as its new customer communications management (CCM) platform. ValueMomentum’s insurance domain expertise and its strong knowledge of OneShield’s platforms made it stand out in the selection phase for a skilled QA partner.

HAI Group and its partners took a phased approach, beginning with around 10 months of blueprinting, analyzing the insurer’s business processes and requirements and mapping them to the OneShield system to identify areas that required configuration and customization for the insurer’s specific needs. The team worked along an aggressive timeline to ensure that business needs were continuously being met and that all lines of business could be moved over to the new systems within the next few years.

“We’re excited about the technology upgrade and the improvement to our team’s internal efficiency, but for us, the most exciting thing is to be able to provide better results to our policyholders through modern systems and engagement channels,” said Bernie Odoy, HAI Group’s Chief Technology Officer.

As soon as the project moved past the requirements phase, ValueMomentum worked with HAI Group and OneShield in a sprint model, conducting functional testing and providing feedback across multiple lines of business and value streams.

ValueMomentum’s QA team played a pivotal role across the entire modernization process. The team dove into understanding the insurer’s requirements, conducting functional testing across the entire project life cycle, and assisting with user acceptance testing. The ValueMomentum team worked closely with the development teams, testing the functionality components as they were developed and starting end-to-end testing in April 2024. At every step of the modernization project, ValueMomentum’s team continues to play a critical role in the modernization effort, handling integration testing, regression testing, and testing of new features, even after golive. Any issues uncovered in production are then tested by ValueMomentum’s team in a lower environment and fixed.

The project was launched in January 2023 and went live for its first two lines of business, general liability and excess, in October 2024. Starting with two lines of business enabled HAI Group to ensure the transformation was completed successfully so that additional lines of business could be rolled out more quickly in 2025.

Moving from a legacy system to a modern, cloud-based core system and CCM platform has enabled HAI Group to offer a better user experience to internal business users, leading to greater efficiency and more time to focus on specific customer needs. The platform upgrade has also paved the way for a better user experience for customers and agents and for future integration with improved user portals. In addition, early results have already shown strong improvements to HAI Group’s quoting process.. As additional lines of business are migrated to OneShield, the insurer anticipates even greater returns on investment.

“Our legacy system lasted 30 years, and we intend for the next one to last that long, too,” Odoy noted. “ValueMomentum has been committed to the project as much as our own employees have. The way they’ve become part of our core operations team is indicative of that; they’ve learned alongside our team to ensure that our new platform is consistently performing as it needs to in order to support our policyholders effectively. This project succeeded thanks to the commitment of our team, combined with the dedication and knowledge of our partners.”

title: Large P&C Carrier Reduces Leakage With Claims Analytics
meta_description: Learn how a global (re)insurer developed a scalable claims analytics framework to reduce claims leakage and improve adequacy.

headings.text: Large P&C Carrier Reduces Leakage With Claims Analytics
Controlling Claims Leakage: The Four Elements of Severity Conservation
Specialty Carrier Reduces LAE With Intelligent Document Processing

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, United States
Established a scalable analytics framework for high-value claims use cases
Improved claims processing efficiency and reduced costs
Reduced claims leakage
Improved reserve adequacy
Enhanced proactive detection of high severity or potentially fradulent claims
AnalyticsClaimsFeatured
The client is a large global P&C insurance and reinsurance carrier offering commercial, specialty, and select personal lines of business.

To reduce claims leakage and improve customer satisfaction, the insurer wanted to redefine its approach to claims severity assessment and fraud detection. Rather than working with a thirdparty vendor to detect fraud and severity signals after an issueemerged, the insurer wanted to move beyond traditional rulesbased processes and combine structured claim attributes with AI-driven analysis of unstructured content.

In its previous workflows, the claims organization found that critical indicators of claim complexity litigation risk, or reserve adequacy were often locked in free-text documents or supporting claim documentation. This meant the insurer had to rely on manual review and interpretation of these documents, hindering a consistent ability to identify emerging severity or suspicious claims patterns early in the life cycle.

By operationalizing its ability to unearth insights from unstructured data, the insurer’s goal was to proactively identify claims requiring early intervention, improve reserve accuracy, prioritize claims for specialist or special investigation unit review, reduce claims leakage, and accelerate claim resolution. This required establishing a scalable analytics foundation that could ingest, process, and analyze both structured and unstructured data to quickly and reliably generate explainable severity and fraud risk scores.

ValueMomentum was already working with the insurer for policy system  maintenance, so the carrier knew ValueMomentum could help jump-start its analytics capabilities. Impressed by the combination of analytics skills and deep domain expertise showcased in a series of claims-focused analytics demos, the carrier decided to collaborate with ValueMomentum on this initiative, starting with two high-impact use cases: severity propensity and fraud detection.

The project launched for a single specialty line of business in November 2025 and was delivered in June 2026. The scalable foundation will be extended for additional products and portfolios. ValueMomentum both designed and implemented the end-to-end analytics platform on a modern, cloud-native architecture using AWS tools like S3, Bedrock, and Cloudwatch as well as Databricks and large language models(LLMs) like Claude. The solution combines traditional machine learning techniques with advanced natural language processing (NLP) and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) to operationalize the insurer’s vast stores of structured and unstructured claims data.

ValueMomentum was able to greatly accelerate the processing of unstructured data by creating an intelligent processing pipeline. Instead of sending every document to an LLM, ValueMomentum developed a multi-stage analytics framework that applied NLP techniques, domain-specific dictionaries, and a comprehensive claims ontology to identify high-value claim narratives and extract meaningful business signals related to litigation, liability disputes, fraud, and more. Then, only the most relevant notes and documents were analyzed using an LLM to derive deeper contextual insights, summarize claims histories, identify severity and fraud indicators, and generate explainable risk signals that claims professionals can use to make faster, better claims decisions.

Establishing a unified analytics framework that combines structured claims data with insights from unstructured sources like claims adjuster notes, investigation reports, legal correspondence, and more has provided the insurer with a scalable foundation for AI-driven decision-making across the entire claims organization. Thereusable claims ontology, AI models, and unstructured data processing framework can all be leveraged across lines of business to drive better decision-making.

Streamlining the approach to manual review has reduced the cost and time devoted to processing unstructured data, freeing up expert claims professionals’ time to focus more on highest risk claims. In addition, the client is better able to detect potential severity escalation earlier, proactively identify claims with indications of fraud, improve reserve adequacy, reduce claims leakage, improve claims handling efficiency, and more effectively triage claims that require specialist review.

Core Platforms

Founded in 1913, NJM is a leading provider of property and casualty insurance in the Mid-Atlantic region. Though NJM began as a workers’ compensation insurance company, their reputation for outstanding services and commitment to meeting their customers’ needs led to rapid growth and successful expansion into multiple lines of business across different states. NJM currently offers auto, homeowners, renters, condo, and umbrella insurance to individuals, and workers’ compensation, commercial auto, and commercial general liability insurance to businesses. NJM is headquartered in West Trenton, New Jersey and employs approximately 2,500 employees.

With the goal of addressing the coverage needs of new and existing customers, NJM decided to expand their commercial offerings to include Business Owners Policy (BOP) and Commercial Umbrella insurance (CUMB) in line with their strategic goal to become a full-service, multi-line regional carrier.

To roll out these new lines of business, NJM decided to expand upon the existing Guidewire platform for BOP/CUMB policy administration and Quadient Inspire for the CCM platform to develop industry standard and custom carrier-specific forms. The end-to-end initiative included creating BOP and CUMB on the Guidewire InsuranceSuite (Policy, Billing, Claims) as well as integrating back office solutions such as documents and financial systems to support the administration of the products. The vast scale and inherent complexity of the program prompted NJM to seek an IT services partner who not only excelled at the technical implementation, but would also offer specific expertise in building and rolling out commercial insurance products.

NJM conducted an RFP process to identify an IT services vendor to support their implementation. Having already worked with ValueMomentum on Quality Assurance and Business Analysis on prior engagements, NJM invited ValueMomentum to participate in the RFP process. After learning about VM’s deep insurance domain knowledge, NJM selected ValueMomentum to be the trusted partner for the implementation of BOP and CUMB. Jozsef Szoke, AVP at NJM, further explains, “ValueMomentum was primarily selected because of their strong understanding of the commercial insurance business, their demonstrated ability to transform a high-level business vision into lower-level business requirements, and their capacity to implement those requirements.”

NJM program managed the implementation and collaborated closely with VM on both PolicyCenter and Documents implementations across three phases (Discovery, Inception, Development) and 6 development sprints.

During the initial stage, NJM worked closely with the business to define requirements and shape the vision for BOP and CUMB offerings. Based on the requirements, NJM then put together an implementation plan. As per the plan, NJM created a product launch questionnaire and underwriting For more information, visit www.valuemomentum.com risk questionnaire, as well as completed product rating algorithm walkthroughs and third-party vendor data analysis. Leveraging VM’s knowledge of Verisk’s ISO Electronic Rating Content (ERC), NJM formulated a framework for measuring deviations from standard insurance loss costs, rules, and forms. This approach helped the company design a product offering that would not only address current market needs, but also be simple to maintain. Ultimately, NJM was able to efficiently implement the new lines in PolicyCenter, establish Predictive Modeling for BOP, and create agent-facing digital experience. Furthermore, NJM rolled out a Producer Distribution Management System (PDMS) to manage producer/ agency onboarding and incentive management.

For Documents, NJM implemented a series of forms, reusable standards, and development practices on the Inspire platform. NJM also drew from ValueMomentum’s technical and insurance-specific expertise to develop reusable assets that would accelerate development. Additionally, a data transformation layer was developed to integrate data from Guidewire PolicyCenter.
Working as one team, NJM and ValueMomentum executed the project over 13 months, successfully setting the groundwork and meeting the timelines for NJM to roll out BOP and CUMB lines.

“This has been a very successful partnership from which both parties have benefited,” Szoke elaborates. “NJM has gained from ValueMomentum’s knowledge in commercial lines, while ValueMomentum has benefited from NJM’s decision to entrust ValueMomentum with a major strategic initiative—a first for NJM, as we’ve never relied on a single partner for the implementation of new lines of business in PolicyCenter.”

Over the coming months, NJM will go live with BOP and CUMB and will roll out the new lines of business to the 6 states in which the company operates. Additionally, NJM will begin to leverage a new distribution channel – independent agencies – to offer the competitive and comprehensive products that their customers demand and expect.

By leveraging ValueMomentum’s commercial insurance and technical expertise to implement the new BOP and CUMB lines, NJM has made significant progress in becoming a regional, full-service and multi-line carrier capable of catering to the needs of both new and existing customers.

meta_description: Why and how did Pekin Insurance migrate their data to Snowflake's Cloud Data Warehouse? Here's a hint: good partnerships were a key success factor.

headings.text: Pekin Insurance Accelerates Decision Making with Snowflake’s Cloud Data Warehouse

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, USA
One-half reduction in owning and operating costs, year-over-year
Ability to accelerate decision-making through increased data accessibility and near real-time report generation
Significantly improve data platform uptime to drive business agility and employee productivity
Data

An innovator since its founding in 1921, Illinois-based Pekin Insurance provides a complete portfolio of personal and commercial insurance, including a full spectrum of life offerings as well as P/C and health. Pekin’s over 800 employees serve more than 900,000 policyholders in 21 states. With combined assets of $2 billion, Pekin supports a distribution network of 1,500 agencies and 8,500 independent agents.

As part of their enterprise-wide Digital transformation, Pekin had undergone a Cloud migration as well as data modernization, which included implementing Hadoop as their data platform. However, because data was still being hosted on-prem, there were significant limitations in data accessibility, which resulted in prolonged wait for insurance rewriting queries and delays in daily report production. As a consequence, Pekin also struggled to derive the right value from their data and reports.

As Pekin was already working closely with ValueMomentum for the overall enterprise transformation initiative, including the initial Data and Cloud Migration, Pekin turned to ValueMomentum as a trusted partner for their migration to Snowflake.

“ValueMomentum knows our current data framework, challenges, and platform really well,” elaborates Josh Edwards, Head of Data Science/Director of Data Management. “As we look at our deadline, ValueMomentum, being a trusted partner, is very well suited to jump right in and help us achieve our goal.”

The project began in June 2020 with the bold goal of completing implementation by October 2020. ValueMomentum was engaged to assist Pekin through the Development, Pre-Production, and Production stage. This included designing the infrastructure, security, network, data movement, and validation process. Going in, Pekin had two major concerns: (1) lack of internal experience using Snowflake and (2) the possibility of data breaches, as migrating to Snowflake would require the transfer of highly sensitive data.

With the help of ValueMomentum, Pekin designed multiple architecture diagrams and proof-of-concept to ensure the security of the migration. Pekin was also able to efficiently migrate not only their historical data load, but also their ongoing daily data load—a complex process that required converting thousands of tables in multiple programming languages into SQL before loading them into the Snowflake database. Moreover, the rigorous documentation provided by ValueMomentum allowed Pekin to seamlessly transfer knowledge between the teams as well as keep communications consistent throughout the project.
Through close collaboration with the ValueMomentum team, Pekin was able to overcome the project’s challenging timeline, and is now on track to complete their migration to Snowflake by December 2020.

For Pekin, the initial investment driver was cost-savings—with a one-third predicted reduction in functional operational costs, the migration to Snowflake is predicted to pay for itself by year end. In addition, as a cloud-based solution, Snowflake can store historical data efficiently and endlessly, as well as scale elastically, easily connecting with existing tools at Pekin.

Speaking to the overall project, Edwards explains, “With ValueMomentum’s expertise, we were able to migrate our data platform from on-prem to the Snowflake AWS. This migration will allow Pekin to shift significant resources from maintaining the data platform to quickly creating business insights and value for our business partners.”

By allowing Pekin to generate reports near real-time and derive valuable insights from their data for agile decision making, the Snowflake migration will put Pekin one step closer to their goal of becoming a truly digital insurance company. Looking forward, Edwards explains, “Pekin is driving towards a data-driven culture, and this platform [Snowflake] is the lynchpin of our transformation.”

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, USA
Ability to offer all Auto coverages on Guidewire
Enabled agility and flexibility for the development, maintenance and servicing of Auto products
Accelerated speed-to-market for entering into new states
Core Platforms

An innovator since its founding in 1921, Illinois-based Pekin Insurance provides a complete portfolio of personal and commercial insurance, including a full spectrum of P/C, health, and life offerings. Pekin Insurance’s over 800 employees serve more than 900,000 policyholders in 21 states. With combined assets $2 billion, Pekin Insurance supports a distribution network of 1,500 agencies and 10,000 independent agents.

Pekin Insurance has been undergoing an enterprise-wide digital transformation project known as PIVOT (Pekin Insurance Virtual Overall Transformation) for almost a decade. The program was designed to meet Pekin’s desire for growth in the P/C market, and involved migrating their P/C lines of business from legacy systems to Guidewire. Pekin predicted the move would streamline internal workflows for improved efficiency, accelerate the development pipeline for delivering new products to market, and cut the cost of maintaining several independent legacy systems.

Pekin worked with its implementation partner, a major IT consulting firm, to roll out Auto and Deluxe Business Owners Policy in its first Guidewire release (R1) in 2017. Subsequent R2 and R3 releases—rolled out in 2018 and 2019 respectively—followed with the same partner for Workers’ Comp, Homeowners and Umbrella. While this partner worked on the rollout of R4 for Commercial Package Policy, Pekin wanted to add more manpower to the project to accelerate the completion of the Auto product line on Guidewire. In August 2019, Pekin turned to ValueMomentum, a vendor partner who has been supporting Pekin in other areas of the business, to lead the final R5 major phase of their Guidewire rollout. This phase included Motorcycle and Recreational Vehicle policies, which were to be migrated to Guidewire in conjunction with a major expansion of service into four new states.

Key factors in Pekin’s decision were ValueMomentum’s knowledge of Pekin’s tools and architecture, an open approach to collaboration, and ValueMomentum’s proven commitment to delivery excellence at cost efficiency.

The R5 rollout included end-to-end implementation of RV and Motorcycle policies, which currently accounts for approximately $5M in premium, on Guidewire PolicyCenter, BillingCenter, and ClaimsCenter. This entailed gathering the business requirements, converting each policy from the legacy system into Guidewire, and integrating them into Pekin’s software ecosystem, while simultaneously testing the new implementation. These phases were divided into work streams, which included project management, business analysis, development, configuration, integration, third-party integration, and rating.

Pekin collaborated closely with ValueMomentum and the vendor partner leading R4, especially through the development phase, since system codes had to be shared between the vendor teams. At the peak of development, the project team comprised approximately 29 onsite and offshore staff which included a project manager, technical architects, developers, and business analysts.

The project was rolled out successfully in 9 months, on time and under budget, with minimal to no defects to the code base. The focus on close collaboration among the vendor teams to deliver for Pekin’s specific needs, and the mutual understanding of Guidewire’s software ecosystem for future development were key factors of success. Commenting on ValueMomentum’s collaboration with both Pekin and the other vendor team, David Whitesell, AVP, IT and Guidewire Program Director at Pekin Insurance said, “You can’t tell if a person is a Pekin employee or a contractor from ValueMomentum because everyone worked as one team.”

With Motorcycle and RV now in Guidewire, Pekin can complete the last major phase of their much larger effort to migrate all P/C policies from their legacy systems. Now, policies can be written, issued, and renewed within a single environment that is automatically connected to billing and claims, allowing much greater flexibility and less room for human error than their legacy systems. This more efficient framework also facilitates rapid development of new products, enhancing Pekin’s ability to meet the demands of its customers with speed, for instance with new predictive modeling. On top of that, the overall cost of ownership has decreased, as Pekin replaced multiple outdated systems with Guidewire.

On the successful partnership with ValueMomentum, David Whitesell added, “ValueMomentum really stepped up to the plate to lead this Guidewire R5 rollout project. They brought a great team, coordinated well with a competing vendor, helped develop the Guidewire expertise of the Pekin team and successfully delivered for Pekin.” Going forward, Pekin will continue to lean on ValueMomentum for further stabilization as well as additional enhancements to their Guidewire systems.

Reconciled and migrated over 3,000 legacy forms spanning Personal, Commercial and Workers’ Comp P/C lines.
Gained a scalable, flexible, cloudfirst enterprise CCM platform
Core Platforms

An innovator since their founding in 1921, Illinois-based Pekin Insurance provides a complete portfolio of personal and commercial insurance, including a full spectrum of P/C, health and life offerings. Pekin’s over 800 employees serve more than 900,000 policyholders in 21 states. With combined assets of $2 billion, Pekin supports a distribution network of 1,500 agencies and 8,500 independent agents

Like many established carriers, Pekin is undergoing an enterprise-wide transformation initiative to streamline and automate multiple processes, including document generation. At the outset, the insurer struggled with antiquated mainframe-based legacy forms generation applications that required IT intervention to make even the smallest adjustments to a form.

“With our legacy processes it could take us nearly three weeks to generate a single document,” says David Whitesell, Assistant Vice President of IT. “Also, the costs and risks of maintaining the outdated onpremise system were mounting as we were unable to rapidly respond to market shifts in an increasingly competitive landscape.”

To empower business users while simultaneously reducing costs and risks, Pekin decided to adopt a cloud-enabled customer communications management platform. They selected SmartCOMM, by Smart Communications, for enterprise CCM, along with Hyland’s OnBase, for storage. Concurrently, the larger transformation effort included migrating core systems to Guidewire.

As Pekin required tight interactions between SmartCOMM, OnBase and Guidewire, as well as integrations with other internal and external systems, a strategic IT integration partner was needed. In particular, Pekin sought a partner with deep knowledge of the insurance industry and expertise with all of the related solutions and subsystems. Also critical was the ability to embrace Pekin’s “one team” approach by working closely with internal employees and business integration provider, Deloitte.

“Initially, we engaged a supplier that we discovered was a poor fit,” Whitesell says. “Luckily, our company was familiar with ValueMomentum due to other projects and brought on their Customer Communications Management Services team for our initiative. This proved a very wise choice.”
To launch enterprise CCM, Pekin established an aggressive 12-month timeline.

ValueMomentum set to work identifying all the core, adjacent, and dependent systems, both internal and 3rd party, as well as determining the best tool for program development and delivery. Next, they designed a scalable, cloud-first architecture by suggesting the best applications for the technology stack. This included leveraging API-enabled MuleSoft for connecting SmartCOMM and Guidewire.
Using agile methodology, ValueMomentum designed an effective test-and-learn framework for developing and continuously improving the resulting CCM solution.

With ValueMomentum’s assistance, Pekin’s IT and P/C business users have reconciled and converted about 3,000 existing static forms onto the platform. This involved migrating all of Pekin’s Personal and Commercial P/C lines as well as Workers’ Comp to enable generating policy, claims, billing and other correspondence. Moving forward, ValueMomentum will assist Pekin’s Life and Health divisions with migrating onto the platform.

“Our new enterprise CCM uses business rules to automatically generate forms dynamically and includes modern capabilities such as auto references, auto computations and auto prefill,” Whitesell says. “The platform infuses flexibility into our business and enables our company to quickly develop new products or make changes to existing ones.”

Today, Pekin has reduced the former three-week documents generation turnarounds to less than a week, for a 67%improvement in process efficiency. Further, new form authoring time has improved by 15% with a new form comparison tool helping to reduce cosmetic defects by over 10%.
“What’s more, by adopting a cloud-first CCM platform, we’ve reduced costs by 29%,” says Whitesell.

“Overall, the initiative has been a great success,” he adds. “ValueMomentum has demonstrated their expertise whilecontinuously going above and beyond. They’ve helped us deliver all of the functionality we wanted and meet all of our goals.In short, ValueMomentum has been a great organization to work with.”

title: Pekin Insurance Enhances Statistical Reporting & Data Verification

headings.text: Pekin Insurance Enhances Statistical Reporting & Data Verification
Pekin Insurance Accelerates Decision Making with Snowflake’s Cloud Data Warehouse

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, USA
Realized a net savings of over $100,000
Reduced data verification time by at least 75%
Eliminated regulatory risks arising from poor data quality, inaccuracies and submission delays
Data

An innovator since their founding in 1921, Illinois-based Pekin Insurance provides a complete portfolio of personal and commercial insurance, including a full spectrum of P/C, health and life offerings. Pekin’s over 800 employees serve more than 900,000 policyholders in 21 states. With combined assets of $2 billion, Pekin supports a distribution network of 1,500 agencies and 8,500 independent agents

Like many insurers offering workers’ compensation policies, Pekin became increasingly burdened by significant overhead costs, and faced associated regulatory compliance risks, resulting from mandated monthly unit statistical reporting (stat reporting).

In particular, Pekin is required to file stat reports with the National Council on Compensation Insurance (NCCI) and the Wisconsin Compensation Rating Bureau (WCRB). “Extracting the appropriate transaction data from our legacy core systems and reformatting it into the necessary bureau data feeds was a chronic headache,” explains Joan Hatler, Enterprise Data Steward. “Our data processing capabilities were increasingly insufficient, resulting in dedicating a staff member to manually verify and reconcile data records for about 60 hours a month.”

It was all so cumbersome that completing a data feed was typically delayed until just hours prior to the deadline, making stat reporting inherently stressful. “Plus, any hiccups meant other employees, such as commercial lines raters and actuaries, needed to take time away from their jobs to assist,” Hatler adds.

In addition, the existing system was unable to generate the data feed needed by Pekin’s claims department for filing workers’ comp subsequent report of injury forms (SROI reporting). As this is also a mandatory monthly task, nearly a day of staff time was dedicated to manually completing SROI forms.“Consequently, our company’s overall costs and regulatory risks grew with each monthly reporting period,” says Hatler.

As Pekin was undergoing a significant digital transformation across their landscape, including adopting the Guidewire core systems suite, the insurer sought a reporting solution that also integrated with their other new systems. “We turned to our strategic IT partner, ValueMomentum, to leverage their expertise and experience,” Hatler says.

The project began with an evaluation of existing processes and statutory requirements to determine the various types of data feed challenges. Then, ValueMomentum collaborated closely with Pekin to develop a plan to create an end-to-end process for automating stat and SROI reporting.

“We really appreciated ValueMomentum’s attention to detail throughout the process,” Hatler says. “Their development team posed insightful questions that helped us address a variety of concerns for creating an effective and intuitive solution that was easy to use.”

ValueMomentum engineered a solution to streamline and automate information extraction and data feed creation to meet NCCI and the WCRB specifications. This was accomplished with tools such as Microsoft SQL Server, Microsoft SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS), IBM Rational, Microsoft Visual Studio and Atlassian Jira.

With Pekin’s modernized solution, stat reporting data feeds take only about 30 minutes to create and are automatically generated 15-20 days prior to NCCI and WCRB due dates. In addition, vastly improved data quality, along with an intuitive business user interface, has slashed verification time to less than 16 hours per month.

“Previously, we needed to verify and reconcile about 40 percent of the records per month in order to create the NCCI and WCRB data feeds,” Hatler says. “That translated to about 50,000 records. Now, it’s less than 3 percent, or fewer than 4,000 records.”
Further, the data feed created by the new solution also contains the necessary SROI reporting information, eliminating the former manual claims task altogether.

As the new system enables multiple employees to refocus from tedious data support chores to higher-value businesscritical tasks, Pekin is realizing considerable net benefits. “We’re saving over $100,000 versus continuing with our former processes,” Hatler says.

“In addition, we’ve addressed a significant regulatory risk and relieved workplace stress,” she adds. “We’ve also gained a fully automated data process that will seamlessly integrate with our other modernized systems, as they go live. For us, the outcome is a tremendous success.”

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, USA
Unlocked 1.5 billion P/C policy and billing records dating back to 1996
Accelerated time-to-market by 70%, reducing new product introductions from 18 months to about five
Eliminated shadow data factories and a 5-year reporting backlog to significantly reduce risks and boost business productivity
Data

An innovator since its founding in 1921, Illinois-based Pekin Insurance provides a complete portfolio of personal and commercial insurance, including a full spectrum of P/C, health and life offerings. Pekin Insurance’s over 800 employees serve more than 900,000 policyholders in 21 states. With combined assets of $2 billion, Pekin Insurance supports a distribution network of 1,500 agencies and 10,000 independent agents.

Focused on transforming its business to compete in the ever-changing ecosystem-driven economy, Pekin Insurance began a sweeping modernization initiative that included adopting Guidewire for policy, claims and billing. However, it quickly encountered various data availability roadblocks.

“We stored most data on our legacy mainframe, which was so difficult to access that our culture became accustomed to waiting for data,” explains Kim Wienzierl, Assistant VP of IT Data, Infrastructure and Delivery. “There were also lengthy delays with gaining new insights due to a five-year backlog of report requests. As a consequence, hidden data factories proliferated, generating inconsistent data and increasing corporate risk.”

To turn the situation around, the insurer embarked on a massive data transformation effort. Since its existing four-person legacy data team was insufficient for the effort, Pekin Insurance conducted an expansive talent search. It sought expertise in Hadoop-based data platforms, along with supporting systems such as master data management, data modeling and business intelligence.

However, attracting talent quickly proved challenging, prompting the insurer to turn to an IT solution provider for technical skills. “During the first six months with the originally selected provider it became apparent they lacked the resources and skills we needed,” recalls Wienzierl.

“This led to considering ValueMomentum, which was already a trusted partner in other areas of our IT organization,” she continues. “We conducted the same rigorous assessment of a vendor and discovered ValueMomentum’s Data team supplied the scalable, mature and collaborative solution we required.”

With ValueMomentum contributing just over half of the individuals on the 53-person implementation team, the new platform was completed in a matter of months, including extracting, reconciling and transferring 1.5 billion P/C policy and billing records dating back to 1996.

To do so, the team leveraged tools such as MuleSoft for data integration; Hortonworks (now Cloudera) for the Hadoop platform; Orchestra Networks for master data management; QlikSense for BI dashboards; and tools like SSIS, Attunity and Sqoop for transferring data between the old and new platforms.

“During our SAFe [Scaled Agile Framework] implementation process, we corrected 14 significant data flaws, leading to considerable accuracy improvements and risk reductions,” says Wienzierl. “For example, when it came time for the Guidewire deployment team to convert personal auto, homeowners and workers compensation, 6,000 records with errors were uncovered and fixed. Naturally, we expect similar situations as conversions continue.”
Today, Pekin Insurance’s new platform includes 2500 Hadoop tables that give business users about 50 (and growing) intuitive self-service dashboards for gaining analytic insights.

“We’ve eliminated the reporting backlog and some of the hidden data factories while enabling Guidewire conversions to occur three times faster,” Wienzierl reports. “In addition, the combination of our new data platform and Guidewire has cut new product introductions from 18 months to only about five.”

According to Wienzierl, perhaps the most important outcome is the resulting cultural transition. “Instead of accepting insufficient data quality, our business users are so engaged and excited that they request new capabilities every day,” she says.

Moving forward, Pekin Insurance’s data team will continue advancing the platform and start migrating it to the cloud. The team will be driving greater cost efficiencies and enable innovation by leveraging native-cloud capabilities from Amazon Web Services (AWS). “ValueMomentum has contributed significantly to our success,” says Wienzierl. “We operate as one team – collaborating, learning and evolving quickly as needs arise.”

“The benefits from choosing ValueMomentum as a strategic IT partner go beyond the productivity we’ve gained,” she continues. “ValueMomentum’s collaborative, can-do approach has contributed immeasurably to the satisfaction of the employees on my team. As we’re distant from technology hubs, having happy employees is critical for retaining our advanced data talent. That’s invaluable to us.”

headings.text: Pekin Partners with ValueMomentum for Multi-State Expansion on Guidewire Cloud
Pekin Insurance Drives Business Expansion with Guidewire PolicyCenter
NJM Grew Commercial Lines with Guidewire PolicyCenter Coverages
Global P&C Insurer Drives Automation with OpenText Exstream & Guidewire PolicyCenter

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, United States
Q1 2023: Pekin Insurance’s Utah growth metrics increased, achieving more than 50% of its annual target
Increased market presence and risk diversification through geographic expansion
Successfully implemented Guidewire Cloud
Streamlined project execution methodology for future state rollouts
Core Platforms

An innovator since its founding in 1921, Illinois-based Pekin Insurance offers a portfolio of health, life, personal, and commercial lines of business. Pekin Insurance’s nearly 800 employees serve more than 900,000 policyholders in 22 states. With combined assets of over $2 billion, Pekin Insurance supports a distribution network of 800+ agencies and 8,800+ independent agents.

Pekin Insurance identified the need for expansion of its commercial lines into new territories to fuel growth and mitigate risks. Its goal: a swift, efficient expansion into Utah without compromising quality.

“To be successful, Pekin Insurance must grow and must do so profitably,” said Joel Jackson, Pekin Insurance’s SVP and COO. “State expansion is a key to both goals. As we expand our footprint, we make our products available to a larger market, naturally increasing our premium income. Additionally, the diversification of risk plays a tremendous role in our profitability.”
The insurer’s targets included five pivotal commercial lines of business (LoBs): commercial auto, business owners’ policy, workers’ compensation, commercial package policy, and commercial umbrella.
Enterprise-wide, Pekin Insurance aimed to transition its core platforms from on-premises to Guidewire Cloud to accelerate overall project delivery time and reduce the burden of future state rollouts.

Pekin Insurance first formed a project execution team comprising a program manager, R&D manager, business subject matter experts (SMEs), business analysts (BAs), an actuary, technical architects, and the release and quality leads. Team members collaborated from the outset to allow parallel development of the product model.

With this new team structure and ValueMomentum’s help, Pekin Insurance began to migrate its on-premises systems to Guidewire Cloud and adopt Guidewire’s SurePath guided implementation approach. The team first utilized pre-existing and standardized content on the Guidewire platform to streamline state requirement review and analysis.

The Actuary team then worked alongside the BAs to develop rates concurrently with the product model and forms. They further implemented Guidewire Predict, enabling them to deploy pricing models that expedited their development timeline.

The program team introduced a pre-UAT/early start of UAT with end-to-end testing conducted by the quality assurance (QA) team and SMEs. The QA team was able to test functionalities simultaneously while identifying critical defects at an early stage. Consequently, both the QA and UAT phases were significantly shortened.

The new execution approach, combining a cross-functional product model development with Guidewire’s SurePath methodology, expedited the Utah rollout by developing all five LoBs simultaneously. Thus, Pekin Insurance was able to complete all development work within eight months.
Pekin Insurance’s 2023 growth metric for Utah is on track to exceed initial targets, with Q1 results greater than 50% of the company’s 2023 annual growth goal.

Importantly, the insurer created a repeatable project execution approach for future state expansion with increased operational efficiency and cost reduction from Guidewire Cloud platform capabilities. Pekin Insurance is on track to expand into an additional state in Q2 2024, with plans to implement (at least) one state per year through 2030.

As we expand our footprint, we make our products available to a larger market, naturally increasing our premium income. FeaturedProduct

Founded in 1875, Red River Mutual provides insurance coverage across Canada for businesses, farms, and homes. The insurer is committed to meeting Canadians’ needs as they evolve with competitive insurance products. Red River Mutual has been recognized as one of Insurance Business Canada’s Top Employers every year since 2019 and was named a Manitoba Top Employer in both 2025 and 2026.

Red River Mutual wanted to ensure that its technological foundation was able to keep up with the needs of its business strategy. From an application perspective, this meant being able to address growing security, compliance, and release speed expectations across its Guidewire core systems and other digital platforms with DevSecOps best practices.

Red River Mutual developed a strong proof of concept (POC) for the foundational frameworks it needed to modernize its application delivery model. These included embedding security earlier into the development life cycle, automating and standardizing CI/CD pipelines where possible, ensuring end-to-end visibility, and building a scalable DevSecOps foundation for future initiatives.

To bring the POC to life, the company wanted to partner with an organization that could review the POC, advise on additional best practices or improvements that could be added to the plan, and help get the plan into production quickly.

Red River Mutual wanted a partner with both DevSecOps experience and a keen understanding of insurance enterprise architecture, including Guidewire systems. The insurer also wanted a partner with the industry knowledge required to add insights where needed — not just provide additional resources to the project. As a Guidewire PartnerConnect Consulting partner at the Select level and proven DevSecOps experience, ValueMomentum stood out during the assessment phase.

The project productionized a DevSecOps pipeline for Red River Mutual’s Guidewire and Spring Boot-based applications. The solution standardized CI/CD pipelines using Jenkins on Microsoft Azure, integrated with Jira for traceability and governance, and aligned application delivery with enterprise security and compliance standards. ValueMomentum helped create an agent deployment pattern to maximize the efficiency of running DevOps pipelines in parallel.

The collaborative team implemented a shift-left approach to ensure that all code being written is analyzed for security vulnerabilities early on. These security controls integrate SAST, SCA, and secret scanning, with Guidewire Quality Gates embedded directly into the development and deployment workflows. The ValueMomentum team delivered comprehensive knowledge transfer and documentation to empower the Red River Mutual team to independently scale the DevSecOps foundation to drive the company’s future strategic initiatives.

Successfully putting the DevSecOps framework into production has not only enabled a scalable, secure foundation for Red River Mutual’s future development efforts, but it has also delivered an accelerated, more predictable release cycle with significantly reduced manual intervention and application security risk.

By automating parts of the development life cycle, Red River Mutual has given its team more time to focus on other tasks while remaining in the loop on deployments with the visibility provided through Jira. The reusable patterns have accelerated future application onboarding while the API-driven architecture supports easy expansion of integrations.

“While we had already begun prototyping our DevSecOps journey, we worked with ValueMomentum to benchmark what we had created against industry standards, enabling the collaborative team to bring a leading-edge DevSecOps foundation into production,” said Brad Powell, Director of Enterprise Solutions at Red River Mutual. “This effort was the result of a collaborative partnership. ValueMomentum analyzed what we had, understood where we wanted to go, and provided augmentations to our plan; they didn’t just add bodies to the implementation.”

Investing in a modern DevSecOps framework has helped Red River Mutual achieve more consistent value streams and catch issues and security risks much earlier in the process, giving the company more time to properly address any problems without impacting IT’s commitments to its business partners.

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, United States

Pre-built 50+ integrations to streamline the agent experience
Rolled out workers’ comp in two new states
Achieved 80% straight-through processing for conversions
Accelerated speed to market both for new products and new geographies
ClaimsFeatured

The client is a New England-based mutual property and casualty carrier. In business for over 200 years, the company works with hundreds of agency partners to cover homeowners, drivers, and businesses with personalized policies.

With a legacy claims platform nearing two decades old, the insurer was facing inconsistent service quality, high support costs, and a growing level of operational risk. To enhance its operations, better enable scalability and business agility, and provide a better user experience to its adjusters and customers, the insurer decided to invest in a modern claims system.

Moving from a cumbersome legacy system to a modular architecture would allow the client to launch enhancements and products more rapidly and respond to market changes as they emerge. The insurer planned to move to a cloud-native platform as part of its long-term digital transformation strategy and overall business scalability.

To bring this goal to fruition, the insurer turned to its long-term strategic partner, ValueMomentum. ValueMomentum worked closely with the carrier on all planning and execution activities for the initiative, which was completed after 24 months of development and system integration testing. After the completion of a twomonth proof of concept stage, the team identified business needs along the entire claims life cycle during a one-month discovery phase.

This was followed by a month-long design phase that, leveraging ValueMomentum’s PRIME framework accelerator, produced a highlevel solution and architecture plan, as well as the non-functional requirements. Built on a cloud-native, Spring-based microservices architecture, the solution uses Camunda for workflow, configuration-based Java frameworks for the transformation layers and user interface, Hi Marley for text-based claims processing, One Inc. for claims payments, and RESTful APIs for secure integration with third-party platforms. The containerized environment was built with enterprise-grade security in mind leveraging LDAP and Azure AD.

On top of the challenge of designing and deploying a new solution, the project included challenges in the form of outdated peripheral systems and 20 years of accumulated technical debt. The insurer’s in-house development approach helped provide the flexibility, fast turnaround, and intense focus on quality and performance needed for the project to succeed. The combined project team’s disciplined execution approach ensured a stable, on-time go-live to achieve the organization’s business goals.

The launch of the modular claims platform has not only led to an enhanced customer experience, but it has also improved operational security and efficiency while cutting down on technical debt. The insurer’s cycle time for first-party auto and homeowners claims has been reduced from 20 days to under 14 days, while forms development time has gone down by 94%, from four hours to only 15 minutes. In addition, document upload speed has risen 60%.

Moving to a cloud-native architecture has prepared the insurer to scale as needed to meet emerging client needs and evolving market trends while embedding security into the carrier’s technical foundation. These improvements are driving not only enhanced speed to market but reduced overall total cost of ownership, better enabling the insurer to bring modern services and coverage to policyholders that align with market changes and evolving consumer needs.

Our client is a renowned, century-old Midwest insurer offering a wide range of products, including auto, business, crop, home, life, renter’s insurance, and more. It is also a prominent underwriter of farm insurance with a team of 1,200 employees and 450 agents.

Transitioning to a cloud-based platform was critical to streamlining operations, minimizing manual data entry, and eliminating outmoded templates. As part of its long-term vision, the client aimed to expand into online business and penetrate new markets with innovative insurance products.

To achieve this transformation, the insurer required a partner proficient in implementing the SmartCOMM platform, adept at requirements gathering and form migration, and capable of providing strategic guidance for the digital transition. The insurer’s aim was to ensure that this transformation aligned with the company’s forward-looking strategic initiatives.

The insurer partnered with ValueMomentum to leverage our expertise with the SmartCOMM platform for a comprehensive implementation attuned to the company’s evolving business needs. The process began with an in-depth discovery phase, working closely with the client’s business team to glean requirements and guide knowledge transfer.

headings.text: Specialty Carrier Reduces LAE With Intelligent Document Processing
Fortune 500 Insurer Optimizes Subrogation Recovery With Predictive Modeling
Smarter Claims Assignment With Graph-Based AI
Claims Reimagined: What a Modern Claims Organization Looks Like in 2026

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, United States
Cut manual data entry time by 80% and reduced LAE
Standardized claims submission and classification process for better accuracy
Improved risk management and claims processing speed
Established framework for business-driven AI implementation
Standardized TPA ingestion for claims submissions
AIClaimsFeatured

The specialty insurer is part of a larger property and casualty mutual insurance company based in the Midwest. It writes multiple lines of business, including professional liability, environmental, property, financial, and excess casualty, and continuously rolls out new lines of business to support customers.

The client wanted to modernize its claims processes, automating where possible and reducing manual workflows. The insurer knew that this investment would not only improve data accuracy and enhance operational efficiency, but also reduce loss adjustment expense (LAE) and help the organization transform claims into a strategic lever for continued growth.

Manual claims data extraction from emails and attachments was time-consuming, not to mention prone to human error and inconsistencies. These documents and emails were not in a standard and consistent format as every TPA sent the information in a different format.

There was also a lack of quality control with the existing system; the automation in place extracted data directly from emails and input it as First Notice of Loss (FNOL) without a standardized data validation process. Manual classification processes were also leading to misclassification across claim types, along with inconsistent data handling and policy validation across claims.

Having worked with ValueMomentum previously as a strategic partner on complex modernization and data projects, the insurer knew that ValueMomentum had the claims domain knowledge and the technological prowess to guide the move from manual processes to AI-driven claims workflows. ValueMomentum helped the insurer define an intelligent claims workflow approach to infuse AI-powered data extraction into its claims processes.

A focal point of the effort was using intelligent document processing (IDP) to extract both unstructured and structured data of all file formats from emails and attachments, no matter which TPA the submission came from, then conduct intelligent field mapping with mandatory claim type classification. Using a hybrid AI strategy, the project implemented context-aware structured data extraction with a dynamic metadata tagging and contextual enrichment protocol. The data was then ingested into a standard FNOL structure that was used for FNOL creation directly into Guidewire ClaimCenter.

The IDP solution was integrated with the insurer’s specialty portal to enable a systematic review process with human-in-the-loop validation prior to FNOL creation. In addition, ValueMomentum ensured that the structured data format would be consistent across all claims to avoid misclassifications and reduce the margin for error. Mandatory claim categorization (e.g., cybercrime, professional services, etc.) with automated date and state code conversion and verification with proper formatting was implemented to ensure that all claims data and FNOL creation followed a taxonomy standardized by claim type.

Infusing IDP and automation across the claims management life cycle helped the insurer cut its manual data entry time by 80% and reduce its LAE. It also created a more consistent process and format for extracting structured data from complex documents and streamlined the workflow from email receipt to FNOL creation.

Mandating a human review step within the automated process helped the carrier ensure accuracy prior to FNOL submission, while standardizing claims type classification across all specialty lines has helped reduce misclassification. paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, United States
Consolidated multiple quoting portals into a single Strategy Quoting Application
Enabled customer self-service
Improved the performance of its applications
Optimized its API foundation to quickly add new partners and distribution channels
Distribution
The client is a specialty insurer based in the Midwest with more than 100 years of experience underwriting both personal and commercial lines of business.

As part of its 2023 strategy, the insurer wanted to enable the rapid rollout of new products while providing an enhanced customer and agent experience, both in terms of making new features quickly available and in overall application performance.

The insurer had a broad range of applications to support quoting, portals, and core capabilities that needed to be streamlined to improve efficiency as well as the user experience for customers and agents. These included six applications for quoting, legacy portals, a portal specifically for personal lines, a microportal for quick pay, and a Guidewire-based portal for producers.

All of these applications, as well as the integrations between the insurer’s systems and strategic partners’ platforms, embedded insurance partners, and other platforms, had left the insurer with an overly complex back end involving more than 14 engagement applications and on-premises core systems with more than 45 end points.

Due to the monolithic nature of the existing application architecture, it became challenging for the insurer to add new features and onboard new partners. In addition, speed, agility, availability, scalability, performance, and security were all becoming increasing concerns as the user base continued to grow.

The insurer decided to use its quote consolidation effort as an opportunity to streamline its existing integrations and enable automated delivery where possible to accelerate its delivery, enhance the customer and agent experience, and improve its embedded insurance offering.
The insurer turned to ValueMomentum to consolidate the fragmented technical landscape, its varying and sometimes redundant business logic, and numerous integrations.

The insurer first underwent a discovery phase to analyze its application ecosystem and how it worked with the Guidewire core system, how the API life cycle was managed, what technology platforms were involved, and the existing implementation process. Applying ValueMomentum’s Cloud-Native Integration Framework allowed for simpler integration with third-party providers and enabled configuration-based integrations.

Next, ValueMomentum’s application engineering team recommended a solution architecture for each area that focused on how to enable the organization’s business goals, including an engagement API for each of the 14 different engagement channels that could communicate with a streamlined and business-aligned API layer.

Using ValueMomentum’s Domain API Reference Solution enabled the teams to move forward with a domain-driven design that allowed for partner-specific customization with considerations such as scalability and API governance built into the framework. Deploying ValueMomentum’s customizable, pre-built CI/CD scripts also helped the project team with faster deployment and infrastructure automation.

The teams utilized a Microsoft Azure container to enable the Kubernetes-based API layer, .NET to design the framework, and the Dapr platform for the API template. The design of the new API layer, including the discovery phase, took eight months to complete.

This project succeeded in simplifying the back-end integrations for the carrier’s engagement channels and partner platform access and improving the portal experience for agents and customers. Building out API life-cycle automation and tools such as API templates gave the insurer a pathway to future scalability.

The optimized application infrastructure provided the insurer with a modern, flexible, and resilient API-driven platform that will allow the company to bring products and features to market quickly as well as accelerate its partner onboarding.

The API life cycle is now automated from creation and design all the way through management and publishing, and the API template provided the insurer’s team with pre-built components that automate non-functional and infrastructure concerns while enabling consistent, accelerated, and configuration-driven implementation.
Thanks to the new application and API layer foundation, the carrier is better positioned to expand its business rapidly, integrate more readily with partners’ platforms, and grow its market share.

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Specialty Insurance, United States
Streamlined submission clearance by 25%
Increased submissions managed by 40%
Integrated over 1,350 forms with the core system
Exceeded profitability targets by two years with a gross written premium of $545 million in its second year
Application Engineering

The specialty insurer is part of a larger property and casualty mutual insurance company based in the Midwest. It writes multiple lines of business, including professional liability, environmental, property, financial, and excess casualty, and continuously rolls out new lines of business to support customers.

The insurer embarked on a large-scale modernization initiative to enable its specialty lines business to expand profitably and efficiently. The goal was to establish the foundation for an endto-end specialty underwriting platform and operating model that could eventually orchestrate the diverse and judgment-intensive workflows that define specialty insurance, going beyond the capabilities of traditional policy administration systems.

An effective underwriting workbench solution for the nuanced risk evaluation of specialty lines necessitated both flexibility and contextual understanding. To enable these capabilities, the insurer set out to evolve from a rules-based model to a forms-driven, orchestration-led underwriting approach — a conceptual model where multiple underwriting functions, services, and processes could be coordinated centrally.

In the existing workflow, underwriters relied heavily on emailbased submissions and static PDFs, which led to inconsistencies, inefficiencies, and long cycle times. The insurer was especially focused on developing a configurable environment in which submissions, documents, and workflows could interact dynamically, providing underwriters with greater control, visibility, and decision support without heavily depending on IT. As an initial step toward its orchestration-led vision, the carrier prioritized building two foundational capabilities — submission management and forms management — to digitize intake, clearance, and document control.

The insurer partnered with ValueMomentum to co-engineer purpose-built solutions for underwriting, rooted in the specific needs of the specialty market, flexible integration, and deep integration with the carrier’s existing core systems. The initiative began with submission and forms management applications as the initial building blocks of the underwriting workbench.

The submission management system digitized the intake, clearance, and triage process, replacing email-driven workflows with structured digital submissions. It provided underwriters and operations teams with clear visibility into submission status, automated clearance checks, and configurable assignment logic, reducing delays and ensuring consistent handling of broker-submitted risks. The forms management library centralized more than 1,350 specialty forms and endorsements across multiple lines of business, introducing features for version control, tagging, and clause comparison. This ensured that underwriters always worked from the latest approved forms and could easily retrieve or adapt templates for new products or jurisdictions.

Both applications were built on a modern, modular architecture leveraging React for an intuitive user interface, .NET microservices for business orchestration, and Postgres as the data store. The solutions were deployed on AWS, using AWS Lambda for event-driven processing and integrated through MuleSoft APIs with the insurer’s Guidewire core system, rating engines, and document repositories.

The architecture emphasized configurability, enabling business users to modify clearance logic, workflow steps, and form templates without IT intervention, and flexibility to ensure the systems’ ability to scale alongside the insurer’s growing product portfolio. In addition, both solutions serve as the technological foundation of additional workbench capabilities such as appetite guidance, risk scoring, and broker collaboration.

The implementation of the submission management system and forms management solutions marked a major milestone in the insurer’s underwriting workbench journey. Both systems went live within four and a half months of the project launch; configurable workflows, reusable components, and seamless integration with the insurer’s Guidewire core system have enabled the insurer to add a new line of business to the system every month and manage the entire submission life cycle within one engagement platform.
This move toward a full underwriting workbench enabled the carrier to exceed its profitability target by two years, achieving a gross written premium of $545 million in the platform’s second year.

The submission management system has brought digital structure, transparency, and control to a previously fragmented, email-based process. Underwriters can now track submissions in real time, apply standardized clearance logic, and accelerate broker response cycles, with a 40% increase in submission intake efficiency and a 25% reduction in clearance turnaround time. The forms management library has provided the insurer with a single source of truth for all specialty forms and endorsements, eliminating duplication, reducing versioning errors, and enabling faster product updates while maintaining compliance.

Beyond efficiency gains, the initiative provided the insurer with a configurable, cloud-native foundation that can evolve to support future specialty capabilities such as AI-assisted risk scoring, appetite alignment, and broker collaboration. This first step in executing its underwriting workbench vision has already enabled the insurer to move from manual, document-driven workflows to a more orchestrated, insight-led underwriting experience.

headings.text: Super-Regional Carrier Accelerates Commercial Lines Business Growth With Guidewire Cloud Platform
Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho Enables Business Agility With Successful Guidewire Cloud Platform Migration
Farm Bureau Insurance Company of Idaho Drives Agility With Guidewire InsuranceSuite Modernization
Pekin Partners with ValueMomentum for Multi-State Expansion on Guidewire Cloud

paragraphs: HomeCase Studies
HomeCase Studies
Insurance, United States
Cut businessowners quote and bind time to under 10 minutes
Pre-built 50+ integrations to streamline the agent experience
Rolled out workers’ comp in two new states
Achieved 80% straight-through processing for conversions
Accelerated speed to market both for new products and new geographies
Core PlatformsGuidewire

The insurer is a midsize super-regional carrier that offers auto, property, life, crop, farm, and business coverage. In operation for 100 years, the insurer is headquartered in the Midwest and supports commercial lines policyholders in nearly 20 states.

As part of its strategic growth initiative, the insurer embarked on a modernization program that would not only move the organization onto more scalable, cloud-based solutions, but also streamline technology processes to enhance underwriting efficiency, increase quotes per agent, provide additional self-service functionality to their captive agent network, and lead to increased profitability.

The initial goals of the program were to modernize the insurer’s policy administration system (PAS), reduce manual integrations and legacy customizations, consolidate applications into a common platform, and enable more business agility and better scalability to support organizational growth goals.

To achieve these goals, the insurer wanted to begin by simplifying the new business quote and submission process as well as increasing straight-through processing (STP) capacity. Both capabilities are pivotal for increasing the number of policies in force and improving the ease of doing business for carrier representatives. In addition, the client wanted to improve its product offerings to better meet the needs of its policyholders. Business outcomes outlined for the program included a multi-state expansion for workers’ comp, faster speed to market, enhanced product bundling capabilities, and more self-service options for policyholders.

The insurer was previously live on a different core system, but it knew that its growth goals required a modern, cloud-based system. The client selected Guidewire Cloud Platform, which required a full PAS transformation, including migrating the entire existing book of business onto Guidewire.

In parallel with the PAS replacement, the client set out to redesign the overall agency engagement experience, adopting a “client-first design” mindset to better align with future customer and agent experience aspirations for both customers and agents

ValueMomentum was already a strategic partner for the insurer, having assisted with multiple initiatives previously. The project team consisted of 88 ValueMomentum employees and 35 associates from the insurer, with an additional 35 shared resources, both business and IT teams, from the carrier. The team designed and implemented the framework to migrate existing data for four commercial lines of business from the insurer’s previous core systems to Guidewire Cloud Platform using tools including Guidewire Policy Migration Tool and Informatica. Leveraging Guidewire Standards Based Templates (SBTs) enhanced the efficiency of implementing client-specific deviations that met the insurer’s business needs.

The program was conducted in a phased approach, with the first release for businessowners, workers’ comp, commercial auto, and commercial umbrella taking place from January 2024 to September 2025. Additional rollouts for new states are planned for these lines of business for completion in January 2026. In subsequent releases, the insurer plans to roll out commercial package policy (CPP) and agribusiness policy.

This core transformation effort streamlined the new business quote and submission process and enhanced producers’ ability to conduct their work. The updated system includes more than 50 integrations, providing more avenues for representative engagement and simplifying the process of adding new distribution channels.

On top of a better agent and customer experience thanks to the faster, more seamless experience, the carrier is now achieving 80% STP for conversions. In addition, its quote and bind time for businessowners policies has been reduced to under 10 minutes.

A month after the first release, the insurer migrated an additional seven states onto the new PAS and rolled out workers’ comp in two new states. This initiative was a major step in the insurer’s five-year growth strategy. The core modernization has not only yielded better STP rates and speed to market, but also made it easier for the insurer to further modernize its digital experience for agents and customers as well as continue its multi-state expansion for lines of business such as workers’ comp

On top of a better agent and customer experience thanks to the faster, more seamless experience, the carrier is now achieving 80% STP for conversions.

This core transformation effort streamlined the new business quote and submission process and enhanced producers’ ability to conduct their work. The updated system includes more than 50 integrations, providing more avenues for representative engagement and simplifying the process of adding new distribution channels.
On top of a better agent and customer experience thanks to the faster, more seamless experience, the carrier is now achieving 80% STP for conversions. In addition, its quote and bind time for businessowners policies has been reduced to under 10 minutes.

This initiative was a major step in the insurer’s five-year growth strategy. Insurance, United States

FeaturedJutro

The insurer is a midsize super-regional carrier that offers auto, property, life, crop, farm, and business coverage. In operation for 100 years, the insurer is headquartered in the Midwest and supports commercial lines policyholders in nearly 20 states.

As part of its business strategy, the insurer wanted to expand its commercial lines presence to match its robust personal lines market share. The client knew that driving this growth would require heavy investment in a better, more modern digital experience for agents, policyholders, and internal stakeholders.

With a heavy personal lines presence, the insurer wanted to make the move to selling commercial lines seamless for its captive agent base. In order to do that, the carrier decided to develop a modern, dedicated quote and bind portal for commercial lines that would improve the sales process for these additional products.

Since commercial lines are more complex than personal lines by nature, the client wanted to streamline workflows and focus on ease of use for its digital touchpoints. The goal was to deliver self-service options wherever possible, implement straight-through processing (STP) at a higher rate, deliver small commercial quotes in 8-10 minutes, and ensure policy issuance in mere hours for non-STP scenarios.

The client decided to take a platform-led approach to its digital experience goals. Since the insurer operates on Guidewire PolicyCenter, it made sense to leverage the capabilities of Guidewire Jutro Digital Platform (Jutro) to simplify necessary integration with the company’s nearly 50 third-party data providers to provide as much data pre-fill as possible.

After a vendor selection phase, ValueMomentum was chosen to collaborate on the implementation thanks to its strong Guidewire knowledge, deep insurance expertise, and a thorough roadmap for the implementation (including training on the newly released Jutro platform). Due to the criticality of digital experience for driving commercial lines growth, the project team built business outcomes directly into the program and tracked them throughout the implementation.

The insurer took a phased approach to rollout and experience development, going live with four lines of business in the first release. Since the Jutro platform was a newer feature, Guidewire took the lead for release one, while ValueMomentum led quality assurance (QA) efforts and invested in training its workforce on Jutro. After the successful go-live of the first release, ValueMomentum took over experience development for the second release. Leveraging an AI-led development approach powered by Github Copilot on top of Jutro’s capabilities, ValueMomentum was able to gain 30% efficiency across the development phase, which is slated for completion in August 2026.

The commercial lines modernization effort and digital experience creation with Jutro has helped the insurer improve both its experience and its operational efficiency, including reaching nearly 17% STP for new business. By six months after go-live of the first release, conversion renewals reached 80% STP; now they are at 92% STP.

Additionally, as part of this commercial lines effort the insurer decided to work with ValueMomentum for product rationalization, consolidating nearly 28 bundled endorsements down to seven core offerings. Each of these offerings will be supported by the digital experience created using Jutro, a shift that has created a scalable, secure foundation for enhanced agent and customer experience. This improved experience will play a pivotal role in helping the insurer drive its commercial lines expansion goals.
